**What the interface is, what it must become, and the numbers to build it from — 2026-08-17.**

Three documents now describe this project's state. `audit.md` is what is **broken**, `GAPS.md` is what is
**absent**, and this one is **how the interface works and how to build the rest of it**. It exists because
the interface is where the largest single hole in the game is: the inventory family is genuinely good, and
*everything outside it* — main menu, world select, world create, pause, settings, death — does not exist at
all, so a new world is currently a recompile and a settings change is a text-editor edit.

Eleven agents produced it in one pass: six researched, one constructed mock-ups from the real artwork, and
**three independent reviewers audited the result** — one on the data, one on the design, one on whether the
engine can actually run it. Their corrections are folded in below rather than left at the end, because
several of them contradict the sections they correct.

---

## 0.1 How to use this file

**Do not read it end to end.** Use the generated index above.

- Building a screen? Read **§0.4 (the rules)** and **§0.6 (the build order)**, then §5.
- Touching the HUD? §0.4, then §6.
- Need a number — a sprite size, a colour, a slot origin? **Do not read prose for it.** Three
  machine-readable files hold it: `assets/ui/ui-atlas.json` (576 sprites, sizes, nine-slice borders),
  `assets/ui/ui-palette.json` (221 measured colours with the file and pixel each came from) and
  `assets/ui/ui-screens.json` (measured geometry for 24 reference screens and 9 of ours). §2, §3 and §4 are
  the human-readable tour of those three.
- Wondering what already exists? §1, which is mechanical and complete.

**Provenance rule.** Every number in §2–§4 was measured off the artwork on disk, not recalled. Where a
famous constant is quoted it was re-verified; the verification is recorded. `tools/extract-ui-spec.ps1`
regenerates the atlas and `-Check` fails if it drifts.

---

## 0.2 The verdict

**The interface specified here can be built on this engine as written, and it requires no Vulkan work at
all** — no new pass, no new pipeline, no new descriptor set, no new upload path. That was claimed by the
specification and then verified line by line by an independent reviewer against the actual renderer. For a
developer who is not a graphics programmer, that is the single most important fact in this document.

What will derail it is **build order**, not capability. The two riskiest edits in the whole plan — migrating
61 `openScreen` call sites, and splitting a 6,130-line `main()` — are pure refactors with **zero
user-visible output**, and the original ordering put both of them *before* the first screen a player could
see. §0.6 fixes that.

---

## 0.3 What was found while writing this

Five real defects surfaced during the pass. They are recorded here because they are cheap and were not
known this morning.

| # | Defect | Where | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Keyboard auto-repeat never reaches the game.** The key callback returns unless `action == GLFW_PRESS`, so `GLFW_REPEAT` is discarded. Holding a key moves focus once, steps a slider once, deletes one character. Clearing a 32-character world name is 32 presses. **Adding key codes does not fix this.** | `engine/src/platform/Window.cpp:330-331` | **Blocking** for menus |
| 2 | **The hotbar, status bars and crosshair draw *on top of* the pause and death screens.** The only gate on drawing them is `openScreen.has_value()`; there is no `alive()` check and pause is not an `openScreen`. The death path closes any open screen, so the else-branch runs and the hearts draw over the death menu. | `Main.cpp:2906`, `:2955`, death at `:4284-4322` | Real, visible |
| 3 | **A sheet-size mismatch only logs and continues**, with a skewed HUD, and the game prefers `hud-reference.png` beside the exe over the repo file. Widening the sheet without regenerating that artefact skews the entire HUD with one console line. | `Main.cpp:1776-1791` | Trap |
| 4 | **Our crafting and furnace slots sit 1 px left of the reference**, and of our own storage column. Traced to a comment in the sheet generator comparing our *frame* origins against the reference's *item* origins — an anchor mix-up. The comment is wrong **and so is the art it produced.** | `tools/make-hud-sheet.ps1:145-148` | Cosmetic, real |
| 5 | **Our double-chest panel is 2 px short** — 176×220 where the reference is 176×222 and the `114 + 18N` rule gives 222. | `assets/textures/hud.png` | Cosmetic, real |

Two more were found by the menu specification and belong to other systems: **save folders are named
`world_<seed>` with nothing else**, so two worlds created on the same seed silently share one save
(`WorldStore.cpp:139`); and **there are zero UI sounds** despite 60 loaded sound events.

## 0.4 The rules — read these before writing any UI code

Six agents wrote §1–§7 independently and **contradicted each other in nine places**. Every contradiction was
adjudicated by a reviewer with the source open. **These resolutions win over anything in the sections
below.** Where a section still says otherwise, it is wrong and this table is right.

### R1 · One art-pixel constant, and container panels shrink 4.19%

> **DONE as of 2026-08-19 — the anchor half of this rule is implemented, and everything written below it is
> now history rather than instruction.** `hud::kArtPixel` (`HudPrimitives.hpp:41`) is
> `kHotbarWidth / kReferenceHotbarWidth`: the hotbar anchor won, exactly as recommended.
> `kPerReferencePixel` **no longer exists anywhere in `game/src`** — measured, zero hits — and `kPixel`
> (`InventoryScreen.cpp:198`) is now an alias reading `= hud::kArtPixel`, not a second definition.
> **Do not unify these again; there is nothing left to unify.**
>
> **What genuinely remains** is only the widening to `pixel(aspect, guiScale)`, and `HudPrimitives.hpp`
> states the blocker at the constant itself: neither term exists yet — nothing clamps the layout to a
> narrow window and there is no `gui_scale` key — and both need the layout to stop being `constexpr`,
> which is a change to every screen rather than to one line. **That is not a five-minute job**, and the
> "five minutes" below refers only to the part already done.

Two constants existed when this was written, both live, 4.19% apart, and two fragments each mandated a
different one: `kPixel = 1.30/166 = 0.0078313` (all eight container screens) versus
`kPerReferencePixel = 1.368/182 = 0.0075165` (hotbar and status bars). **Both reviewers
found this independently and both call it the highest-value five-minute decision in the plan.**

> **The rule.** UI positions are in **screen units**: origin at screen centre, **+Y down**, Y spanning
> −1…+1 over the window *height*, X spanning −aspect…+aspect. The only transform in the pass is an x-scale
> (`Renderer.cpp:2170-2173`).
>
> **One reference GUI pixel is `hud::pixel(aspect, guiScale) = min(2/266.08, 2·aspect/320) × guiScale`
> screen units.** The height term is what the HUD has always used; the width term is the reference's own
> 320-pixel minimum virtual width and is the only thing in the UI that reacts to aspect ratio. Every size
> and offset in this document is written in reference pixels and multiplied by that one function.
>
> **No other file may define an art-pixel constant.** `kPixel` and `kPerReferencePixel` both collapse into
> it, with a `static_assert` tying any survivor to it.

**The hotbar anchor wins** because the hotbar, XP bar and boss bar are all 182 reference pixels wide, so
three future elements need no second constant. **The consequence is that every container panel shrinks
4.19%** (`kPanelHeight` 1.30 → 1.24774). That is a **bug fix, not a regression** — we currently draw the
inventory panel 4.19% too large relative to the hotbar, and every slot centre is derived so hit-testing
follows automatically. It is worth one screenshot check because it moves art that was eyeballed.

**Do this before anything else in §0.6.** Unified later instead, it silently resizes every existing screen
with nothing to catch it. *(Superseded 2026-08-19: the unification is done — see the note at the head of
R1. Only the `pixel(aspect, guiScale)` widening is outstanding, and it is no longer a prerequisite for
anything below it.)*

### R2 · Depth is a sort key, not a depth test

The UI pass has **no depth attachment at all** (`Renderer.cpp:2152`, and the pipeline sets
`depthFormat = VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED`, `depthTest = false`, `depthWrite = false` at `:255, 262-264`). Ordering
is: **which mesh** (`main` → `clipped` → `top`, a fixed order), then **z as a `stable_sort` key within that
mesh**, then **append order** on ties.

So the menu specification's justification — *"a blended fragment still writes depth, so depth must be
strictly ordered"* — is **factually wrong and inherited from a stale comment** at `Renderer.hpp:120-128`.
The conclusion survives; the mechanism does not. **Drop the proposed nine-sub-band depth scheme**: give
every quad on a screen the same depth and append strictly back-to-front, so ordering lives in the code you
are reading rather than a constant table 400 lines away. Reserve distinct depths only where two different
widgets genuinely overlap. **This also corrects `audit.md` §5.3**, which has been amended.

### R3 · Every quad needs 12 indices, and culling must stay

Quads are emitted with **both windings** — `{0,1,2, 0,2,3, 0,2,1, 0,3,2}` at `HudPrimitives.cpp:58, 79, 96,
296`. Back-face culling then rejects exactly two of the four triangles. **This is a correctness requirement,
not a performance one:** the pipeline comment (`Renderer.cpp:262-265`) records that drawing both sides
blends every panel over itself and turns an alpha of 0.55 into 0.80. Anyone "simplifying" to six indices
*and* disabling culling gets double-blended panels everywhere. The cost is 16% more index bytes on UI
geometry and **no extra fill rate**.

### R4 · Build only the rows the scissor keeps

A 44-row settings screen built in full is ~4,100 quads and 722 KB per frame; built to the ~6 visible rows it
is ~650 quads and 115 KB. The difference is a **build-time decision, not a render-path property**, and the
catalogue already does the right thing (`catalogueCapacity()` returns 56, not 1,343 —
`InventoryScreen.cpp:404`). Rebuild-every-frame is otherwise **fine and already proven**: the heaviest mesh
in the game — the inventory plus a 56-cell isometric catalogue — is rebuilt at 60 Hz today and nobody has
complained. Buffers are suballocated from a pooled 32 MB block, so a rebuild costs microseconds.
**Do not build a dirty-flag or persistent-buffer system first;** that is engine work for no measured
benefit. Set `screenDirty` and move on.

### R5 · The settings row is a two-column grid, not a label-and-control row

The specified row put the control on the label's line. **Neither cited Bedrock screenshot does that** — both
put label and value on one line and the control full-width beneath. More importantly the specified geometry
**overflows**: the label column is 114 px and, measured against our own font atlas, `Worker Threads: Main
thread only` is 192 px, `Frame Rate Limit: Unlimited` 161, `Render Distance: 12 chunks` 152. Most
value-carrying labels run into the slider.

> **Use a two-column grid.** Panel **320×176**; content 308 after a 6 px inset; 300 after the scrollbar and
> gap; **two columns of 147 with a 6 px gutter**; control height 20; **row pitch 24**; **6 rows visible =
> 12 controls on screen**, so the 24-row Video tab is two screens rather than seven. Group headers take
> their own 20 px row across both columns.
>
> **Descriptions move into the existing `appendTooltip` on hover and on focus** (`HudPrimitives.cpp:347`) —
> zero new primitives, and it already clamps to the window and flips above the cursor near the bottom edge.
>
> Four labels need shortening to fit 147 px: `Threads: Main only` (107), `Frame Limit: Unlimited` (132),
> `Render Dist: 12 chunks` (127), `Pointer Sens: 1.00×` (111).

At 320 px this panel needs aspect ≥ 1.203 — **narrower than the inventory already requires (1.2765)**, so it
adds no new aspect floor and the proposed bespoke narrowing rule can be deleted outright.

> ⚠ **`ui-mockup-settings-preview.png` shows the *superseded* row design.** It was constructed before this
> reconciliation, so it draws the control on the label's line. The layout above is correct; the mock-up is
> not. Regenerate it with `tools/make-ui-mockups.ps1` once the two-column grid is implemented.

### R6 · One clipped mesh, one scissor rectangle

There is exactly one clipped mesh and one scissor rect (`Renderer.hpp:638-643`, applied at
`Renderer.cpp:2196-2220`), and `top` is already occupied by the debug overlay, the held stack and the
gamepad pointer — and is unclipped. **Two stacked screens therefore cannot both scroll.** State the rule and
obey it: **only the focused screen may scroll.** The alternative is a second clipped mesh, which is renderer
surgery, and this is precisely how a project acquires it by accident.

Related: **the renderer retains whatever mesh was last set.** Copy `rebuildHud`'s ending
(`Main.cpp:2987-2990`), which sets all three unconditionally, rather than the loading loop, which sets one
and gets away with it only because the others are empty.

### R7 · UI sound: one event, two pitches

`SoundEvent::Click` exists (`Sounds.hpp:66`), its stem is loaded (`Sounds.cpp:23`), there is a non-positional
path (`Sounds.cpp:359` `playGlobal`), and it is referenced **nowhere**. It is a fully loaded, entirely
unspent event — and zero UI sounds is the largest single "feels wrong" gap in the whole interface.

> **Play `Click` at pitch 1.0** on button activation (release-inside), cycler step, tab change, list-row
> selection and dialog confirm. **Play `Click` at pitch 0.8** on back, cancel, Escape-pop and the cross
> button — one event, two pitches, confirm and cancel audibly distinct for free.
>
> **Play nothing** on hover, focus movement, keystrokes, scrolling or screen push. Vanilla is silent there
> and a per-hover tick at 60 fps is maddening.
>
> **Do not spend** `ChestOpen`/`ChestClose` (they mean *container*), `Pop` (item pickup), `LevelUp`
> (reserved for XP, which does not exist yet), `Bell`, or `WoodClick` (a world interaction — two meanings
> for one sample is the confusion to avoid). Route through the `sound_volume` bus. ~6 call sites total.

### R8 · The HUD sheet becomes 256 × 1765, once

Two sections each widened the sheet independently and each called its change "the entire change" — one to
256 px wide for new widgets, one to 1765 tall for effect icons. They are compatible but neither knew about
the other. **The final size is 256 × 1765**, changed once, and it requires updating `kSheetSize`
(**`HudPrimitives.hpp:26`**, not `:24`), the assertion at `Main.cpp:1781-1792`, **and both staging scripts**
(`tools/make-hud-sheet.ps1`, `tools/make-reference-hud.ps1`). With 256 px of width the effect-icon grid can
be 14 columns rather than 10. **Make the size mismatch a hard failure** rather than the current log-and-
continue (defect 3 in §0.3).

### R9 · `gui_scale` is a live float, not a restart-only cycler

The two specifications disagreed on both type and liveness. **Resolution: a float slider, applied live.**
The type is settled by `hud::pixel(aspect, guiScale)` already taking a multiplier — a four-step cycler is a
float with a worse interface, and the settings screen already carries twenty-odd float sliders. Liveness is
settled by the fact that the HUD is rebuilt every frame while a screen is open, so a live value costs
nothing **provided `guiScale` is passed into `hud::pixel()` at rebuild time rather than baked into a
`constexpr`** — which is exactly what the proposed signature does. Only `worker_threads` remains
restart-only. One further detail: **if a scale multiplier lands, multiply the gamepad pointer speed by it
too** (`Main.cpp:3126-3131`), or crossing the screen at 2.0 takes twice as long.

### R10 · One authoritative settings key table

`Settings.cpp` parses **44** keys today. This document adds **four**: `fov`, `gui_scale`,
`immediate_respawn` and `subtitles` — **48 total**. Two sections proposed overlapping key sets and one
proposed `gui_scale` twice with different types. There must be **one** `kOptions` table with a
`static_assert` that its size equals the number of keys `Settings.cpp` parses, so the two can never drift.
`subtitles` belongs on the Accessibility tab, which otherwise has only four rows.

### R11 · Small consistencies

- **One `wrapText`, one `appendTooltip(span<string_view>)`.** Two sections specified word-wrap independently;
  assembled as written they would produce two implementations and two tooltip signatures.
- **Citation drift:** where §5 and §1 disagree on a line number, **§1 is authoritative** — it is the section
  that read the file. **Re-measured 2026-08-19 and all four had rotted:** `appendQuad` is at
  `HudPrimitives.cpp:428` (cited :41), `appendText` at `:761` (cited :246), `textWidth` at `:749`
  (cited :234), and `kSheetSize` at `HudPrimitives.hpp:49` (cited :26). A wrong line number is the
  cheapest kind of wrong comment, but **four of four rotting is the measurement that matters**: date a
  citation, or a later reader cannot tell a stale one from a live one.
- **1-art-pixel focus rings and separator rules will render unevenly** — 4 device pixels on two edges of a
  rectangle and 5 on the other two, because our scale is fractional at every common resolution. Make them
  **2 art pixels**, or snap widget rects to device pixels at build time.
- **`Renderer.hpp:389`'s "retired meshes should hover near zero" is wrong** whenever a screen is open —
  steady state is 6–9 with three meshes rebuilt per frame. A future session will read it as a leak.

## 0.5 What this pass deliberately cut

Bedrock's menus carry Realms, Marketplace, friends, achievements, sign-in, profiles and a character
creator. **All of it is cut, permanently.** This is a single-player, personal-use game: it needs to start,
resume, configure and quit. Recording the cut here so a future session does not helpfully rebuild a store.

**The visual language is classic Minecraft**, not Bedrock's modern "Ore UI" — a decision made on three
grounds and endorsed by review: we already draw the classic look (six greys, hard bevels, the 8 px font), it
reuses the panel and slot vocabulary we have, and Ore UI's shell largely exists to organise the very
features just cut. One idea is borrowed from Ore UI — a description line for each settings row — and it
lands in the existing tooltip rather than the row (R5).

## 0.6 The build order

This supersedes the orderings inside §5 and §6, which were written before the feasibility review. The
principle: **nothing that can break what already works may precede a screen the player can see.**

| # | Do this | Why here |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | **Pick the art-pixel constant** (R1). Put it in `HudPrimitives.hpp`; `static_assert` the other against it. | Five minutes, and every number in this document depends on it. Cheapest moment it will ever be. |
| **1** | `engine::Key` gains arrows, Tab, Delete, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown — **plus a keyboard held-timer for auto-repeat** (0.4 s then 0.11 s, matching the pad's existing values). | **The only engine change in the entire plan**, and XS. Without the repeat timer, menu navigation and text editing are unusable and slice 3's own acceptance test passes anyway. **Do not** accept `GLFW_REPEAT` in the callback — it would spam `E`, `Q` and `1`–`9`. |
| **2** | **Widget module, purely additive** — `appendNineSlice`, centred/right/ellipsised text, `wrapText`, `TextField` (with a clipboard wrapper and `Ctrl+V`), `ScrollState`, `Focus`. **Do not migrate the search box yet.** | Additive code cannot break what works. All of it is free functions on plain data, `static_assert`-checkable in the style the repo already uses, and none of it touches `main()`. |
| **3** | Sheet widening to **256 × 1765**, both staging scripts regenerated, **hard failure** on size mismatch. | After 2, because 2's throwaway test screen tells you what art you actually need. |
| **4** | **Pause menu** as a *parallel* `std::optional<ScreenId>` beside `openScreen`, one `else if` branch in `rebuildHud` — **and hoist `saveEverything` out of `Main.cpp:7033-7100` while you are there.** | No stack, no migration, ~1 session, and the first screen a player sees. **The hoist closes `audit.md`'s #1 finding — "no autosave; a crash loses all inventory, chests, furnaces and creatures". That is worth more than every other screen in this document combined.** |
| **5** | **Settings** on the same one-deep model — the `kOptions` table with its round-trip assert, five tabs, and the F-keys retired in the same slice. | The biggest user-visible win. Settings → Confirm needs depth 2; a two-entry array covers it and is not a refactor. |
| **6** | **Death screen and the confirm-dialog pattern.** | Small, independent, and it replaces a silent 1.6-second teleport. |
| **7** | **The screen stack proper** — collapse `openScreen` and `menu` into one. | Now you have three working screens as regression tests and you know what depth you actually need, instead of guessing it in advance. |
| **8** | `world.dat` and a multi-world `WorldStore`, plus a migration for the existing `world_1337`. | Fixes the same-seed save collision. Before the `main()` split, because it is smaller than the split. |
| **9** | The `main()` split → main menu → world select → world create. | Last, because it is the largest edit and every earlier slice makes it smaller. |

**If there is exactly one session:** do 0 and 1 (about an hour together), then build Pause with three
hardcoded quads and no widget module at all — Resume, Options (drawn disabled), Save & Quit. It needs
nothing from slices 2–4, it is roughly 200 lines, **it closes the autosave bug**, and it proves the whole
menu path end to end before a single abstraction is written. If the session goes badly you have lost 200
throwaway lines instead of a half-migrated `main()`.

- **Nothing was built and nothing was run.** The machine was under load; every finding is static. Anything

- **No game source was changed.** The only files written were this document, the three JSON files under

## 1. The UI we have, and how it works

*Written 2026-08-12 by reading source only. **No build was run and the game was never launched** (the brief forbids it), so every number here is read off the code or measured off a PNG on disk. Anything that could only be settled by looking at a frame is marked **[unconfirmable]**.*

**Scope:** our own code — `game/src/hud/`, the screen half of `game/src/Main.cpp`, the renderer's UI pass, the two HUD shaders, the three atlas-building scripts and `assets/textures/hud.png`. Reference art, palette, cell geometry, missing screens and missing HUD elements belong to other fragments.

**The one-paragraph version.** Nine free functions in `game/src/hud/` each return a plain `engine::MeshData` (`engine/include/engine/render/MeshData.hpp:17-20`) of screen-space quads. `rebuildHud` (`game/src/Main.cpp:2887-2990`) concatenates them into **three** meshes — main, clipped, top — and hands them to the renderer. The renderer sorts each mesh's triangles back-to-front on the CPU and replays them in one extra render pass **after** tone mapping, into the swapchain image, **with no depth attachment at all**. Order is the only thing that decides what covers what.

---

### 1.1 The render path, end to end

#### 1.1.1 The chain

| # | Stage | Where | What happens |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A HUD function builds geometry | `game/src/hud/*.cpp` | Pushes `engine::Vertex` into a `MeshData`. **No Vulkan type is visible anywhere in `game/src/hud/`** — the only engine header those files include is `engine/render/MeshData.hpp` (`game/src/hud/Hotbar.hpp:5`, `StatusBars.hpp:5`). |
| 2 | `rebuildHud` concatenates | `game/src/Main.cpp:2887-2990` | Three destination meshes: `hud` (`:2891`), `clipped` (`:2894`), `topLayer` (`:2896`). The `append` lambda (`:2898-2905`) rebases indices by the current vertex count. |
| 3 | Three setter calls | `game/src/Main.cpp:2987-2990` | `renderer.setScreenMesh(hud)`, `renderer.setClippedScreenMesh(clipped, clipMin, clipMax)`, `renderer.setTopScreenMesh(topLayer)`. |
| 4 | CPU painter's sort | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:144-172` (`sortScreenIndices`) | Called by all three setters (`:1202-1219`). |
| 5 | Upload | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:1202-1219` | Each mesh has its own vertex/index buffer pair, re-uploaded whenever the setter is called. |
| 6 | `recordUiPass` | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:2128-2226` | One `vkCmdBeginRendering`, one pipeline, three `vkCmdDrawIndexed` calls. |

#### 1.1.2 Where the UI pass sits among the passes

`Renderer::drawFrame` records, in order (`engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:1413-1438`):

```
recordShadowPass → recordGeometryPass → recordDeferredPass → recordForwardPass
                 → (bloom) → recordToneMapPass → recordUiPass
```

Two consequences that matter more than they look:

- **The UI is drawn after tone mapping, so it is not tone-mapped, not exposed and not bloomed.** A colour written by a HUD function lands in the swapchain essentially as authored.
- **The UI is drawn at full window resolution even when the world is not.** `setRenderScale` shrinks every pass *up to and including the tone map*; the tone map stretches the world back to the window and the UI pass then draws over it at native size (`engine/include/engine/render/Renderer.hpp:275-286`). Text stays sharp at render scale 0.5.

#### 1.1.3 The pass state — and the correction to `audit.md` §5.3

`audit.md:399-417` (§5.3, *"Every blended draw in the forward pass writes depth"*) says of the HUD:

> *"`Renderer.hpp:120-128` admits it in prose: 'a blended fragment still writes depth… That is exactly what the stack on the cursor did to the catalogue behind it. Ordering is the only fix **while the HUD shares the world pipeline**.'"*

**That is now stale for the HUD.** The finding is still correct about `m_trianglePipeline` and the *world's* translucent draws, but the HUD no longer uses that pipeline. The current truth:

| Property | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Pipeline | `m_hudPipeline`, its own object | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:243-266` |
| Shaders | `hud.vert.spv` / `hud.frag.spv` | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:245-246` |
| Depth attachment | **none** — `depthFormat = VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED` | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:249` |
| `depthTest` | `false` | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:250` |
| `depthWrite` | `false` | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:251` |
| Blend | `BlendMode::Alpha` (the `PipelineDesc` default, not overridden) | `engine/include/engine/render/GraphicsPipeline.hpp:50` |
| Cull mode | `VK_CULL_MODE_BACK_BIT` (the default) | `engine/include/engine/render/GraphicsPipeline.hpp:48-52` |
| Colour attachment | the swapchain image, `loadOp = LOAD` | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:2135-2150` |
| Depth in the pass | *"No depth attachment. That is the whole point of this pass."* | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:2145` (comment) |
| Transform | `glm::scale(mat4{1}, {1/aspect, 1, 1})` push constant — no view, no projection | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:2172` |

`hud.frag`'s header comment states the history plainly: *"A blended fragment still writes depth, so every transparent texel of every HUD quad used to reject whatever was drawn later behind it — which cost three shipped bugs in two days and a fourth nobody had noticed. The UI pass has no depth attachment at all now, and order alone decides what covers what."* (`engine/shaders/hud.frag:5-10`).

> ⚠️ **`engine/include/engine/render/Renderer.hpp:120-128` still carries the old prose** and is the doc-comment a future session will read first. It describes a problem that no longer exists. Flagged in §1.9.

#### 1.1.4 The sort

`sortScreenIndices` (`engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:144-172`) is a `std::stable_sort` over **triangles** (index triples), keyed on `max(z)` of the triangle's three vertices, **descending** — largest z first, smallest z last. So:

- **Smaller `depth` = nearer = drawn later = wins.**
- The sort is **per mesh**. It cannot order a triangle in `hud` against one in `top`.
- It is *stable*, so **triangles with equal depth keep their append order**. This is load-bearing: the three faces of a block icon share a depth and rely on it (`game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.cpp:101-235`).

#### 1.1.5 Cross-mesh order

Fixed, and not adjustable by depth: `recordUiPass` draws **main → clipped → top** (`engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:2178-2224`). Anything that must sit over a catalogue icon has to go into `top`; giving it a smaller z in `hud` will not save it.

The clipped mesh is scissored. `setClippedScreenMesh` stores the rectangle (`engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:1207-1212`) and `recordUiPass` converts mesh units → clip → pixels with `(x / aspect * 0.5 + 0.5) * width` and `(y * 0.5 + 0.5) * height`, then restores the full scissor before the top mesh (`engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:2201-2218`). The rectangle comes from `catalogueListBounds()` (`game/src/Main.cpp:2988`, defined `game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:684`).

#### 1.1.6 The vertex format

One `Vertex` for everything in the game (`engine/include/engine/render/Vertex.hpp:16-37`), 32 bytes, `static_assert`ed:

| Field | Type | What the HUD puts in it |
|---|---|---|
| `position[3]` | 3 × float | x, y in screen units; **z is the sort key only** |
| `color` | packed RGBA8 | the tint, multiplied with the texel |
| `uv[2]` | 2 × float | 0–1 within the chosen sheet |
| `layer` | float | **negative values are signals** — see below |
| `surface` | uint32 | always `engine::kVertexSurfaceDefault` for UI |

**`layer` selects the sheet** (`engine/shaders/hud.frag:38-44`):

| `layer` | Sampler | Constant |
|---|---|---|
| `< -1.5` | `fontTexture` | `kFontLayer = -2.0f` (`game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.hpp:29`) |
| `< 0.0` | `hudTexture` | `kHudLayer = -1.0f` (`game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.hpp:18`) |
| `>= 0.0` | `blockTextures[layer]` | any `TextureLayer` value |

Solid colour is done by sampling **`TextureLayer::White = 5`** in the block array (`game/src/world/Block.hpp:6436`) — a 1×1-ish flat white layer. `hud.frag:35-37` warns: *"Reordering that list moves the whole HUD onto whatever lands on that index."* `hud.frag:27-33` also runs the animated-texture swizzle on UI vertices, so an inventory icon of water or fire animates rather than freezing on the frame it was built with.

Sampler is `VK_FILTER_NEAREST` on both magnify and minify, address mode `REPEAT`, with a full mip chain (`engine/src/render/TextureArray.cpp:240-248`).

#### 1.1.7 The rules a new UI element MUST obey

1. **Emit both windings.** Back-face culling is on, and the UI skips the projection matrix that normally fixes winding. Every helper emits **12 indices per quad**, not 6: `{0,1,2, 0,2,3, 0,2,1, 0,3,2}` (`game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.cpp:58-59`). A quad emitted with 6 indices will be invisible roughly half the time depending on the sign of its half-extents. **[unconfirmable which half, without a frame]**
2. **Pick a depth in the existing band table and never reuse one across layers that overlap.** There is no depth buffer; equal depths fall back to append order, which is fragile across a refactor. The bands are listed in §1.4.6.
3. **Decide which of the three meshes you belong to** before choosing a depth. `hud` for the body, `clipped` for anything that must be cut off at the catalogue edge, `top` for anything that must cover the clipped mesh.
4. **Do not assume the depth test protects overlapping sub-parts.** `appendBlockIcon`'s comment still speaks of "the depth test" (`game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.cpp:101-235`); what actually orders its boxes today is the descending sort plus `kBoxStep = 0.00002f` applied per box. The result is the same, the mechanism is not.
5. **Use `TextureLayer::White` for untextured quads, not `kHudLayer`.** An untextured quad gets uv `(0.5, 0.5)` (`game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.cpp:50`); on the HUD sheet that texel is `#C6C6C6`, so the colour comes out at 77.6 %. See defect D5 in §1.9.

### 1.2 The coordinate system and scaling

#### 1.2.1 Units

| Question | Answer | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Origin | Screen centre, `(0, 0)` | `engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:2172` — the only transform is an x-scale |
| +Y | **Down** | `game/src/hud/Hotbar.hpp:22` — `kHotbarCentreY = 0.888f` puts the hotbar near the bottom |
| Y range | −1.0 (top) … +1.0 (bottom), always | the scale matrix leaves y alone |
| X range | −aspect … +aspect | `x` is multiplied by `1/aspect` on the way to clip space |
| Unit | **1.0 = half the window height**, on *both* axes | same |
| Z | 0.0 … ~0.005 in practice; a sort key, nothing else | §1.1.4 |

So a square is a square: equal half-width and half-height give equal pixels. Everything scales with **window height**; nothing scales with width.

#### 1.2.2 The one art-pixel scale

```
kPanelHeight = 1.30f                       InventoryScreen.cpp:147
kPanelPixelSize = {176, 166}               InventoryScreen.cpp:65
kPixel = kPanelHeight / 166 = 0.00783133   InventoryScreen.cpp:155
```

Everything on a screen is `art pixels × kPixel`, and **every position goes through one of two functions**:

- `toScreen(kind, artX, artY)` — `game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:209`, for the right-hand card
- `toBook(artX, artY)` — `game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:216`, for the catalogue card

`toScreen` subtracts `panelPixelHeight(kind) * 0.5f`, i.e. it **centres** the panel vertically, so a taller panel grows both up and down.

Derived values worth having to hand:

| Quantity | Art px | Screen units |
|---|---|---|
| Slot pitch (`kSlotPitchPixels`, `:172`) | 18 | 0.140964 |
| `kSlotHalf` (`:177`) | 9 | 0.070482 |
| Panel half-width `kPanelHalfWidth` (`:197`) | 88 | 0.689157 |
| Panel half-height, standard (`:198`) | 83 | 0.650000 |
| Panel half-height, double chest (`:159,161`) | 110 | 0.861446 |
| Book half-width `kBookHalfWidth` (`:201`) | 73 | 0.571687 |
| `kTooltipTextHeight` (`:179`) | 8 | 0.062651 |

#### 1.2.3 GUI scale

**There is none.** No setting, no hotkey, no multiplier. `settings.cfg` has 44 keys and not one of them touches the UI (`game/src/core/Settings.cpp:170-230`). The UI is a fixed **65 % of window height** at every resolution (`kPanelHeight = 1.30` of a 2.0-tall screen). This is resolution-independent but unadjustable — `GAPS.md` G2.11.

#### 1.2.4 The aspect-ratio limit — **verified, GAPS.md is right**

The two cards are laid out side by side with a 4-art-pixel gap:

```
kCardGapPixels     = 4                                            InventoryScreen.cpp:184
kLayoutPixelWidth  = 146 + 4 + 176 = 326                          InventoryScreen.cpp:185
kInventoryShiftPixels = 326/2 − 176/2 = +75                       InventoryScreen.cpp:190
kBookCentrePixels     = 146/2 − 326/2 = −90                       InventoryScreen.cpp:191
```

Half the block is `163 × kPixel = 1.27651` screen units. The window's half-width is `aspect`. Therefore:

| Aspect | Half-width available | Fits? |
|---|---|---|
| 21:9 (2.333) | 2.333 | yes |
| 16:9 (1.778) | 1.778 | yes |
| 16:10 (1.600) | 1.600 | yes |
| 3:2 (1.500) | 1.500 | yes |
| 4:3 (1.333) | 1.333 | yes, 0.057 to spare |
| **1.2765** | 1.2765 | **exactly flush — the limit** |
| 5:4 (1.250) | 1.250 | **no, clipped both sides** |
| 1:1 | 1.000 | no |
| any portrait | < 1.0 | no |

`GAPS.md` §2.4's *"At any aspect below ≈ 1.277 both cards run off the screen edges"* is **arithmetically confirmed**. **Nothing clamps, rescales or repositions.** `aspect` is passed into `build()` (`game/src/Main.cpp:2941`) but is used only for the full-screen dim quad (`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:718`) and for clamping tooltips (`game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.cpp:347-375`) — never for the layout itself. **[unconfirmable visually]**

The vertical direction is safe: the tallest thing is the double-chest panel at 0.8615 half-height, and the tab strip above a standard card tops out at `−0.65 − 25×kPixel = −0.8458`.

#### 1.3.3 The two enums that must never be reordered

**`StatusIcon` — column order in the 1345 strip** (`game/src/hud/StatusBars.hpp`, read by `StatusBars.cpp:20-22`):

| Column | x | Icon |
|---|---:|---|
| 0 | 0 | HeartEmpty |
| 1 | 10 | HeartFull |

| 4 | 40 | FoodFull |

**`CellState` — column order in the 773 strip** (`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:118-136`):

| Column | x | State | Interior |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | `Craftable` | the panel's own `139,139,139` recess, unchanged |
| 1 | 20 | `CraftableHovered` | that, mixed 0.45 toward white |
| 2 | 40 | `Uncraftable` | `243,74,63` |
| 3 | 60 | `UncraftableHovered` | that, mixed 0.45 toward white |

All four are stamped from the panel's own 18×18 storage tile with only the interior repainted, so every state carries the identical bevel (`INTERFACE.md` §3.1). **`nothing may reorder that enum`** — `cellSheetMin` is `static_cast<float>(state) * kCellSheetPitch`.

#### 1.3.4 The reference-vs-ours fallback

There are **two** copies of this sheet and the game prefers the one that is *not* in `assets/`:

| Priority | Path | Regenerated by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (wins) | `hud-reference.png` **beside the exe** (`build/debug/bin/`, `build/release/bin/`) | `tools/make-reference-hud.ps1` |
| 2 | `assets/textures/hud.png` | `tools/make-hud-sheet.ps1` |

Selection is at `game/src/Main.cpp:1776-1792`; the same pattern applies to `font-reference.png` over `assets/textures/font.png` (`:1798-1811`). Both candidates are size-checked against `kSheetSize` / `kFontSheetSize` and a mismatch **logs an error and carries on** rather than failing the load.

`tools/make-reference-hud.ps1` starts from our sheet and overlays only two things — the **five tabs in both states** (recovered by flood-filling the interior between fill values 98 and 198) and the **ten 9×9 status icons**. Everything else in the proof sheet is still our art.

> ⛔ **`INTERFACE.md` §1.5 records the trap already paid for once:** *"Adding the hopper panel and re-running only the first left the game reading new offsets out of an old image, and every hotbar icon sampled the wrong rows."* **Changing the sheet means re-running both scripts.**

`tools/extract-ui-icons.ps1` is the third script: it crops the 22×25 tab sprites out of a 1280×720 console capture at exactly 3× into `reference/ui-icons/*.png`, which is what `make-reference-hud.ps1` then consumes.

| Grid | 16 columns × 16 rows of 8×8 cells (`kFontCell = 8`, `kFontColumns = 16`, `:35-36`) |
| Mapping | **cell index == codepoint** — Mojang's `ascii.png` layout |

### 1.4 Every screen we have

#### 1.4.1 The list

`enum class Kind` has **eight** members (`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.hpp:29-72`). Many more *blocks* open a screen — a smoker is a furnace, and a barrel, trapped chest, ender chest and stowbox are all chests.

| `Kind::` | Panel y | Panel h | Catalogue? | Craft slots | Result slots | Container slots | Blocks that open it |
|---|---:|---:|:--:|---|---|---|---|
| `Inventory` | 41 | 166 | **yes** | 4 (2×2) | 1 | 0 | none — key/pad only |
| `CraftingTable` | 207 | 166 | **yes** | 9 (3×3) | 1 | 0 | crafting table |
| `Furnace` | 373 | 166 | no | 2 (input, fuel) | 1 | 0 | furnace, smoker, blast furnace |
| `SmithingTable` | 793 | 166 | no | 2 side by side | 1 | 0 | smithing table, grindstone, anvil ×3, *(brewing stand — unreachable)* |
| `Chest` | 959 | 166 | no | 0 | 0 | 27 | chest, barrel, trapped chest, ender chest, stowbox |
| `DoubleChest` | 1125 | **220** | no | 0 | 0 | 54 | a chest paired with a neighbour |
| `Hopper` | 1355 | 166 | no | 0 | 0 | 5 (borrows `Region::Chest`) | hopper |
| `Stonecutter` | 1521 | 166 | no | 1 | **3** | 0 | stonecutter |

Only `Inventory` and `CraftingTable` answer `showsCatalogue(kind)` true (`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.hpp:182`). `isContainer(kind)` is true exactly where `chestSlotCount(kind) > 0` (`:232-248`).

#### 1.4.2 The layout table

`layoutFor(kind)` (`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:284-315`) is a single `constexpr` table. All coordinates are **art pixels, panel-local, origin top-left**:

| Kind | `craftSize` | First craft-slot centre | Result centre |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `Inventory` (the fallthrough) | 2 | (106, 26) | (162, 36) |
| `CraftingTable` | 3 | (37, 25) | (131, 43) |
| `Furnace` | 0 | (63, 25) — fuel at (63, **61**) via `kFurnaceFuelCentreY` (`:319`) | (123, 43) |
| `SmithingTable` | 2 | (45, 43) | (131, 43) |
| `Chest` / `DoubleChest` | 0 | (16, 26) | — |
| `Hopper` | 0 | (52, 43) | — |
| `Stonecutter` | 0 | (28, 43) | (94, 43), then +18 per cut |

Shared constants (`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:172-175`): storage row 1 centre y = **92**, hotbar row y = **150**, first column x = **16**, pitch **18**.

`craftSlotCentre` (`:320`) carries a scar worth quoting: *"A screen with no grid still has slots, and dividing by its grid width is an integer divide by zero — which on x86 is a hardware fault, not a wrong answer. The stonecutter has one input and `craftSize` 0, so opening it killed the process outright."* It now falls back to `width = 1`.

`slotsFor(kind)` (`:339`) is the count actually placed: 1 for the stonecutter, 2 for furnace and smithing, `craftSlotCount(kind)` otherwise.

#### 1.4.3 The catalogue card (the "book")

| Constant | Value | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `kCatalogueColumns` | 7 | `InventoryScreen.cpp:225` |
| `kCatalogueLeft` | `(146 − 7×18)/2 = 10` | `:226` |
| `kCatalogueTop` | 26 | `:227` |
| `kCatalogueBottom` | 160 | `:228` |
| `kCatalogueLabelY` | 15 (the tab-name row) | `:229` |
| `kSearchFieldWidth` | `7×18 = 126` | `:234` |
| `kSearchFieldHeight` | 13 | `:235` |
| `kSearchBorderPixels` | 1 | `:236` |
| `kSearchTextHeight` | 8 | `:237` |
| `kTabPitch` | 25 | `:247` |
| `kSearchExtraGap` | 21 | `:248` |

**Rows:** tops at 26, 44, 62, 80, 98, 116, 134, **152**. The row at 152 has only `160 − 152 = 8` of its 18 pixels inside the card. `catalogueCapacity()` (`:404`) counts it — **8 rows × 7 = 56 cells** — and both drawing and hit-testing honour it: the clipped row is drawn as a shortened quad *and* hit-tested against only its visible height (`catalogueCellAt`, `:607`). `catalogueWholeRows()` (`:416`) counts **7**, and is used only by `catalogueMaxScroll` (`:629`) so that scrolling to the end still lands the last entries in a full row.

**Tabs** are *not* evenly spaced: the first four pack on a 25-unit pitch and Search is pushed a further 21 right, ending at 143 — three short of the card's 146, which is the card's own frame width (`:239-251`). Unselected tabs are drawn from sheet row 721 with `kUnselectedTint{0.72,0.72,0.72,1}` (`:60`) at `kTabDepth`; the selected one comes from row 748 at `kSelectedTabDepth`, which puts it **in front of** the card so it reads as part of it.

**Search** matches at the **start of any word** of an item's name, not anywhere in it — `"st"` finds Stone and Stone Stairs but not Sandstone (`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.hpp:205-208`, implemented `InventoryScreen.cpp:538`). `catalogueItems` takes the whole `CatalogueState` rather than a tab and a string, deliberately, because **three** callers need the identical list: the drawing, the click resolution and the scroll limit (`InventoryScreen.hpp:210-215`).

#### 1.4.4 What `build()` actually draws

`build` (`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:707-754`), called from `game/src/Main.cpp:2938-2951`. It returns the main mesh and fills two out-parameters (`clipped`, `top`). In order:

1. Full-screen dim quad, `kDim{0,0,0,0.55}` at `kDimDepth`, sized `aspect × 1.0` (`:718`).
2. Tabs (catalogue screens only), unselected then selected.
3. The card panel(s) as sprites from the sheet.
4. The catalogue: cell backgrounds → **clipped**; icons and count labels → **clipped**; the tab-name label and the search field → main.
5. Slots: storage grid, hotbar row, craft slots, result slot(s), chest slots.
6. Furnace `FurnaceProgress` indicators — flame at art (55,36) and arrow at (79,36), scaled by `progress.burn` / `progress.cook` (`:143-144`).
7. The held stack at the pointer, into **`top`** at `kHeldIconDepth` / `kHeldCountDepth`.
8. The tooltip for whatever slot the pointer is over, into **`top`** at `kTooltipDepth`.

`game/src/Main.cpp:2946-2956` then adds the gamepad pointer to `top` at depth `0.0004`, height `0.075`, **only when `inputDevice == Gamepad`** — *"Nothing is shown for the mouse: the OS already draws that, and two arrows in the same place is the bug this avoids"* (`:2946-2948`).

#### 1.4.5 Opening and closing

**Opening.** `openScreen` is a `std::optional<Kind>` (`game/src/Main.cpp:2562`).

| Path | Line | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `E` key, pad `Y`, pad `X` | `game/src/Main.cpp:3195-3372`, `:3374-3435` | opens `Kind::Inventory` |
| Right-click on a block where `isInteractive()` is true | `game/src/Main.cpp:4370-4423` | opens the kind for that block; records `openBench`, `openFurnacePosition`, `openChestPosition`, `openChestPartner` |

Opening always: releases the cursor (`setCursorCaptured(false)`), recentres the virtual pointer to `(0,0)`, and plays the container-open sound.

**Closing.** `closeScreen` (`game/src/Main.cpp:2789-2827`) is the **single** exit and does five things:

1. Gives the **cursor stack** back to the inventory, dropping to the world if it will not fit.
2. Gives the **craft grid** back — *except* for the furnace, whose `craftSlots` are only a *view* onto the block (`furnaceToSlots` / `slotsToFurnace`, `:2833-2855`). It still **clears** them, because for one milestone it did not and that was an item-duplication bug: the copies turned up in the next screen's grid (`INTERFACE.md` §1.5).
3. Clears `searchFocused` / `typingSearch`.
4. Plays the container-close sound.
5. Recaptures the cursor.

Triggers: `Esc` (`:3199-3207`), `E` again, pad `B`, pad `Start` (`:3391`).

#### 1.4.6 Depth bands — the master table

Smaller = nearer = drawn later. `game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:21-43` unless noted.

| Depth | Constant | What |
|---:|---|---|
| 0.0050 | `kPanelDepth` (`DebugOverlay.cpp:38`) | debug panel backdrop — **in the `top` mesh** |
| 0.0045 | `kGraphBackDepth` (`DebugOverlay.cpp:39`) | frame-graph backdrop |
| 0.0044 | `kDimDepth` | the world-dimming quad |
| 0.0042 | `kTabDepth` | unselected tabs |
| 0.0040 | `kPanelDepth` | both cards; also `kGraphInkDepth` in the overlay |
| 0.0038 | `kSelectedTabDepth` | the selected tab |
| 0.0036 | `kCellDepth` | catalogue cell backgrounds |
| 0.0035 | `kLabelDepth` | tab-name label; also `kTextDepth` in the overlay |
| 0.003570 / 0.003560 | `kSearchBorderDepth` / `kSearchFieldDepth` | search box border, then recess |
| 0.0032 / 0.0031 | `kCatalogueIconDepth` / `kCatalogueCountDepth` | catalogue icons and counts |
| 0.0030 / 0.0026 | `kIconDepth` / `kCountDepth` | slot icons and counts |
| 0.0012 / 0.0008 | `kHeldIconDepth` / `kHeldCountDepth` | the cursor stack |
| 0.0006 | `kTooltipDepth` | tooltip |
| 0.0004 | (local) `kPointerDepth` (`Main.cpp:2953`) | gamepad pointer |
| 0.00098 | `kIconDepth` (`StatusBars.cpp:85`) | status icons (no screen open) |
| 0.00095…0.00060 | `Hotbar.cpp:51-60` | hotbar frames, tints, icons, counts |
| 0.0001 / 0.0 | `Crosshair.cpp:23-24` | crosshair border, then inner |

> Note the overlay's 0.0050/0.0045 are *behind* `kDimDepth` — which is exactly why `rebuildHud` puts the overlay in the **`top`** mesh rather than the main one (`game/src/Main.cpp:2967-2971`): *"with a screen open the panel was covered and only the text survived; drawn last it sits over everything."* A perfect illustration of §1.1.5.

#### 1.4.7 The non-screen HUD

| Element | Builder | Shown when |
|---|---|---|
| Crosshair | `makeCrosshair()` (`game/src/hud/Crosshair.cpp:54`) | no screen open. Arm 0.021 long, 0.0013 thick, 0.0006 border (`:18-20`) |
| Hotbar | `makeHotbar()` (`game/src/hud/Hotbar.hpp:39`) | no screen open. Slot 0.152, centre y 0.888, width 1.368, top y 0.812 (`Hotbar.hpp:19-28`) |
| Status bars | `makeStatusBars()` (`game/src/hud/StatusBars.hpp:107`) | no screen open **and not creative** (`Main.cpp:2965`) |
| Debug overlay | `makeDebugOverlay()` (`game/src/hud/DebugOverlay.cpp`) | `F5`; goes into `top` |
| Loading screen | `makeLoadingScreen()` (`game/src/hud/LoadingScreen.cpp`) | during world load, via `setScreenMesh` directly (`Main.cpp:2094`) |

Status-bar geometry is derived from the hotbar rather than invented (`game/src/hud/StatusBars.cpp:48-66`): `kPerReferencePixel = kHotbarWidth / 182`, icons 9 of those, pitch 8, rows 10 apart, health/food row just above `kHotbarTopY`, air row one row-pitch above that, outer edge flush with the hotbar's. `airRow()` (`StatusBars.hpp:73-85`) is `constexpr` and splits bubbles into full and bursting on a 30-tick / 2-tick rule.

### 1.5 The slot and cell mechanics as implemented

#### 1.5.1 Regions

`enum class Region` (`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.hpp:103`): `Grid`, `Craft`, `CraftResult`, `Chest`, `Armour`, `Offhand`. `SlotHit` is `{Region region; std::size_t index;}`.

**`Armour` and `Offhand` are dead** — nothing ever *produces* them. **The conclusion holds but the evidence
quoted here was wrong, corrected 2026-08-19:** a grep for `Region::Armour|Region::Offhand` across `game/src`
does **not** return nothing — it returns six hits. Read rather than counted, they are two consecutive `case`
labels at `InventoryScreen.cpp:993-994`, which *consume* the enumerators, plus four comment mentions in
`Survival.hpp` and `Main.cpp`. No code path constructs either one. **A negative claim needs the bare-name
search, not the count** — and stating it as "returns nothing" invited a reader to re-run the grep, get
hits, and conclude the opposite of the truth. `GAPS.md` §2.4 logs this.

#### 1.5.2 Hit-testing

`slotAt(kind, x, y)` (`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:645`) tests, in order: chest slots (if `isContainer`) → the 36 grid slots → craft slots → result slots. Each test is `within(x, y, centre, kSlotHalf)` — an axis-aligned square of half-extent 0.070482 (`:372`). **Cells are square and edge-to-edge**: half-extent 9 art px on an 18 px pitch, so there is no dead gap between neighbours.

Companion predicates:

| Function | Line | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `tabAt` | `:591` | which tab, if any |
| `catalogueCellAt` | `:607` | which catalogue index, honouring `scrollRow` and the clipped bottom row |
| `insideSearchField` | `:636` | over the search box |
| `insideCatalogueList` | `:676` | anywhere over the list — cells, gaps and the empty space below. **This is the destroy bin.** The tabs and the frame are deliberately outside it "so a misjudged click on a tab cannot cost you what you are holding" (`InventoryScreen.hpp:194-197`) |
| `insidePanel` | `:689` | over either card, so an outside-click can be told from a missed slot |

#### 1.5.3 The five operations

All in `game/src/item/SlotOps.cpp` (145 lines), all pure functions on `ItemStack&`:

| Operation | Semantics |
|---|---|
| `leftClick(slot, cursor)` | Same item and room → merge as much as fits. Otherwise → **swap**. |
| `rightClick(slot, cursor)` | Empty cursor → take `ceil(count/2)`. Non-empty cursor → place **one**. |
| `distribute(targets, cursor, rightDrag)` | The drag sweep. Left drag: each eligible slot gets `cursor.count / eligible`, remainder stays on the cursor. Right drag: each gets exactly **1**. |
| `quickMove(from, targets)` | Shift-click. Fills **matching partial stacks first**, then the first empty. |
| `gather(target, sources)` | Double-click. Sources sorted **ascending by count**, so small stacks are consumed first. |

**Shift-click means something different with a container open.** `quickMoveTargets` takes an earlier branch gated on `isContainer` and offers **only the slots that screen shows** — a hopper stores its five in a 27-slot struct and the other 22 are unreachable (`INTERFACE.md` §1.5).

#### 1.5.4 Click ordering in `Main.cpp`

The whole interaction block is `game/src/Main.cpp:3472-3900`. The order is the important part:

1. **Drag continuation first** (`:3643-3677`). If a drag is live and the button is still down, add whatever slot the pointer is over to `draggedSlots` (dedup at `:3649`). On release: if fewer than **2** slots were touched, **rewind** the recorded state and replay it as a plain click (`:3664-3676`).
2. **Double-click test before the drag arms** (`:3856-3859`). `kDoubleClickWindow = 350 ms` (`:2736`), and it must be the **same region and index** as the previous click.
3. **Drag arms only with a non-empty cursor** (`:3882-3885`) — `dragOriginalCursor` is snapshotted so the rewind is exact.
4. Otherwise a plain `leftClick` / `rightClick`, with shift routing to `quickMove`.

State lives in four locals: `DragButton dragButton` (`:2729-2730`), `dragOriginalCursor` (`:2731`), `draggedSlots` (`:2732`), and `lastSlotClick`/`lastClickRegion`/`lastClickIndex` (`:2737-2738`).

#### 1.5.5 The cursor stack

`heldStack` is an `ItemStack` living in `main()`. It is drawn into `top` at the pointer (`kHeldIconDepth 0.0012`, count at `0.0008`), returned on close (§1.4.5), and can be dropped into the world with `Q`.

#### 1.5.6 The catalogue as a source

In **creative** the catalogue is not a recipe book; it is an item source (`game/src/Main.cpp:3722-3766`):

| Input on a catalogue cell | Result |
|---|---|
| Left click | a **full stack** onto the cursor |
| Right click | **one** onto the cursor |
| Shift + click | straight into the inventory |
| Left click on empty list space | **destroys** the cursor stack (left button only) |

In **survival** `catalogue.restrictToKnown = true` and the list is the learned recipe book. Learning is one-way: `craftableItems(inventory, kMaxCraftSize)` is unioned into `catalogue.known` whenever `hudDirty` (`game/src/Main.cpp:4010-4017`) — *"the full grid, so a recipe you could only make at a table is still learned by holding its ingredients."*

#### 1.5.7 Craftable colouring

Each catalogue cell picks one of the four `CellState` sprites (§1.3.3). Hover mixes toward white by **0.45** rather than multiplying, "because red is already at 243 and scaling only clamps the channel carrying the hue" (`INTERFACE.md` §3.1, implemented `game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:515-519`). **In creative the check is skipped entirely** — there are no reds, because everything is one click away.

**Fixed 2026-08-19 (`fx-draw`).** Ordinary slots used to have **no hover state at all**; only catalogue cells did (`GAPS.md` G2.8). Every slot now brightens on hover, and the two quads that do it are the reference's own sprites **read pixel by pixel rather than approximated**: `gui/sprites/container/slot_highlight_back.png` and `slot_highlight_front.png` are each 24×24 nine-slice with `border: 4`, and **all 320 border pixels are fully transparent** — the only ink in either is a 16×16 core of flat white, **alpha 96 on the back sheet, 32 on the front**.

That measurement is what unblocked the fix. It had previously been deferred on the assumption that the brightening had to come from the HUD sheet the way the catalogue's does, which would have needed `tools/make-hud-sheet.ps1` (not `fx-draw`'s file) — but **the sprites carry no shape at all**, so reproducing them needs no art: `game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp` appends two plain untextured quads over the slot interior, at `kSlotHighlightBackDepth` (behind the icon, so a full slot still reads as full) and `kSlotHighlightFrontDepth` (over it, so the brightening lands on the picture and not merely in the gap around it). Both depths are pinned by `static_assert` against the surrounding ladder, and all four asserts were **fault-controlled** — each fires on a deliberately wrong value while the shipped file compiles clean.

The centre comes from `hoveredSlotCentre`, which calls **the same four centre functions `slotAt` hit-tests** rather than a second set of coordinates that agree today; a highlight able to drift from the region that produced it is the "one thing drawn in two places" fault this project keeps paying for. It is drawn **whether or not a stack is on the cursor** — unlike the tooltip, which deliberately hides while carrying — because while carrying is precisely when you need to see which slot you are about to drop into.

---

### 1.6 Text

#### 1.6.1 The atlas and the advances

The sheet is 128×128, 16×16 cells of 8 px, cell index == codepoint (§1.3.5). But the **advance widths are not baked in** — they are **measured off whichever atlas actually loaded**, at startup (`game/src/Main.cpp:1836-1859`):

1. For each of the 128 cells, scan for the **rightmost opaque column**.
2. Advance = that column + 2.
3. A completely blank cell → 4.
4. Space (0x20) is forced to 4 regardless.
5. `setFontAdvances(table)` installs it (`game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.hpp`, implementation `HudPrimitives.cpp:35-38` reads it back through `fontAdvance`).

This is why swapping in `font-reference.png` re-spaces the text correctly without a code change.

#### 1.6.2 The glyph quad

Glyphs are **cropped to `min(advance, 8)` columns**, not drawn at full cell width (`game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.cpp:250-318`). The comment explains why: the font layer has no alpha discard, and under the old shared-depth-buffer pipeline a full-width quad's transparent margin ate the next letter. The crop survives as belt-and-braces.

#### 1.6.3 The exact call

```cpp
float appendText(engine::MeshData& mesh,
                 std::string_view text,
                 float leftX, float centreY,     // left edge, vertical centre
                 float charHeight,               // in screen units
                 float depth,
                 const glm::vec4& color,
                 bool shadow = false);           // HudPrimitives.hpp:94
```

- **Left-aligned, vertically centred.** Returns the width drawn.
- `float textWidth(std::string_view, float charHeight)` (`HudPrimitives.cpp:237`) pre-measures, for centring: every caller that centres does `-textWidth(t, h) * 0.5f` (e.g. `LoadingScreen.cpp:54`).
- **Shadow**: drawn first, offset `kFontShadowOffset = 1.0f` texel down-right, tinted `kFontShadowTint = 0.25f`, at `depth + kFontShadowDepth (0.00002f)` — i.e. one micro-band behind (`HudPrimitives.hpp:42-44`).

#### 1.6.4 What text does NOT do

| Feature | Present? |
|---|---|
| Word wrap | **no** |
| Line breaks | **no** — `\n` is a glyph like any other |
| Colour codes (`§`) | **no** — one `glm::vec4` for the whole string |
| Right/centre alignment built in | **no** — do it with `textWidth` |
| Non-ASCII | **no** — codepoints ≥ 128 fall to `kDefaultAdvance` and sample a garbage cell (`HudPrimitives.cpp:35-38`) |
| Kerning | **no** — advance table only |

### 1.7 Input

Everything is hardcoded in `main()`. **There is no keybinding system, no rebinding, and none of these appear in `settings.cfg`** (`game/src/core/Settings.cpp:170-230` — 44 keys, none of them a binding).

#### 1.7.1 Keyboard

| Key | Effect | Where | Hardcoded? | Documented to the player? |
|---|---|---|---|:--:|:--:|
| `Esc` | close screen if open; else release cursor. **Pressed twice, the second does nothing** | `Main.cpp:3199-3207` | yes | no |
| `E` | open/close `Kind::Inventory` | `Main.cpp:3195-3372` | yes | no |
| `Q` | drop cursor stack (screen open) / drop held item (world) | `Main.cpp:3195-3372` | yes | no |
| `1`–`9` | select hotbar slot | `Main.cpp:3195-3372` | yes | no |
| `Backspace` | delete a search character — **only while `typingSearch`** | `Main.cpp:3162-3181` | yes | no |
| printable keys | typed into the search field via `consumeTypedText()` — **only while `typingSearch`** | `Main.cpp:3162-3181` | yes | no |
| `F1` / `F2` | frame cap down/up. **Does not persist** | `Main.cpp:3362-3371` | yes | no |
| `F3` / `F4` | FOV down/up. **Does not persist** | `Main.cpp:3300-3305` | yes | no |
| `F5` | toggle debug overlay | `Main.cpp:~3260` | yes | no |
| `F6` / `F7` | render distance | `Main.cpp:~3310` | yes | no |
| `F8` / `F9` | spawn a creature | `Main.cpp:3195-3372` | yes | no |
| `F10` | cycle tone mapper | `Main.cpp:~3317` | yes | no |
| `F11` | toggle bloom | `Main.cpp:~3324` | yes | no |
| `F12` | cycle debug view | `Main.cpp:3195-3372` | yes | no |
| `G` | shadow quality | `Main.cpp:~3332` | yes | no |
| `C` | cloud quality | `Main.cpp:~3342` | yes | no |
| `F` | input mode | `Main.cpp:3195-3372` | yes | no |
| `V` | weather | `Main.cpp:3195-3372` | yes | no |
| `Shift` (held) | modifier: quick-move on click | `Main.cpp:3472-3900` | yes | no |
| `Space` ×2 | toggle fly | `Main.cpp:3060` region | yes | no |

**Every row is undocumented in-game.** There is no controls screen, no key list, no tooltip — the only place these exist is the source.

#### 1.7.2 Mouse

| Input | Screen open | No screen |
|---|---|---|
| Left click | slot ops / tab / catalogue / bin | attack, break |
| Right click | slot ops / focus search | use, place |
| Shift + click | `quickMove` | — |
| Left click ×2 within 350 ms on the same slot | `gather` | — |
| Left/right held + sweep | `distribute` | — |
| Wheel | **scroll the catalogue** (catalogue screens only) | change hotbar slot |
| Move | drives `pointerX/pointerY` directly from `window.cursorX()/cursorY()` | mouse-look |

The wheel accumulates fractional notches in `scrollCarry` so a trackpad works (`Main.cpp:3930-3958`). The cursor delta is **read, not consumed**, at `Main.cpp:3073-3076`, because mouse-look further down owns the consume.

Two guards worth knowing:

- `swallowClickUntilRelease` (`Main.cpp:2879`) — the click that recaptures the cursor is spent, and held spent until the button comes up, "so re-entering the window cannot also swing".
- `mouseSettleFrames = 2` (`Main.cpp:3082-3091`) — capturing/releasing teleports the OS cursor, which is indistinguishable from a huge mouse movement; two frames are ignored so mouse and pad do not fight over `inputDevice` forever.

#### 1.7.3 Gamepad

`game/src/core/Gamepad.cpp` + `Main.cpp:3374-3465`. **The pad has no real cursor, so a virtual one is synthesised and drawn** (§1.4.4).

| Pad input | Screen open | No screen |
|---|---|---|
| `A` | synthesised **left** mouse press | jump |
| `X` | synthesised **right** mouse press | open inventory |
| `Y` | synthesised **left** press **with `padQuickMove` set** (= shift) | open inventory |
| `B` | close screen | — |
| `Start` | close screen (**no menu — same non-behaviour as `Esc`**, `Main.cpp:3391`) | — |
| `LB` / `RB` | previous / next catalogue tab | previous / next hotbar slot |
| Left stick | moves the pointer, `kPointerUnitsPerSecond = 1.9f`, **Y inverted into screen space** | move |
| Right stick | scrolls the catalogue, `kScrollNotchesPerSecond = 9.0f` | look |
| Triggers | threshold **0.35** | attack / use |

The pad is sampled **once per frame** at `Main.cpp:3070` — *"so every reader sees the same frame and the trigger edges are found in exactly one place."*

Settings that exist for the pad and have **no mouse counterpart**: `controller_look_sensitivity`, `controller_cursor_sensitivity`, `controller_deadzone`, `controller_rumble`, `controller_invert_y` (`game/src/core/Settings.cpp:200-205`). There is no `mouse_sensitivity` and no `fov` key at all.

#### 1.7.4 The search field's focus rule

The keyboard is stolen **only after the field is clicked** (`typingSearch`, `Main.cpp:3162-3181`). Clicking anywhere else releases it (`insideSearchField`'s doc comment, `InventoryScreen.hpp:222-224`). Query is capped at **22 characters**, and the caret blinks on a **0.6 s** cycle.

### 1.8 The primitives we already have

This is the section a new screen is built from. All in `game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.hpp` / `.cpp`, namespace `game::hud`, all free functions taking `engine::MeshData&` as the first argument.

| # | Function | Line | What it does | Gotcha |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `appendQuad(mesh, cx, cy, halfW, halfH, depth, color, layer, textured)` | `.cpp:41` | One axis-aligned rectangle. `textured=false` forces uv `(0.5,0.5)`. | **Pass `TextureLayer::White`, not `kHudLayer`, when untextured** — see D5. Emits 12 indices (both windings). |
| 2 | `appendSprite(mesh, cx, cy, halfW, halfH, depth, sheetMin, sheetSize, color)` | `.cpp:62` | A rect from `hud.png`, by **pixel** rect. Divides by `kSheetSize` for you. | Uses `kHudLayer` internally (`.cpp:78`). Sheet coords are top-left origin. |
| 3 | `appendQuadCorners(mesh, const vec2 (&corners)[4], const vec2 (&uvs)[4], depth, color, layer)` | `.hpp:76`, `.cpp:87` | An **arbitrary** quad — four explicit corners with four explicit uvs. This is the escape hatch for anything not axis-aligned. | Corner order decides winding for one of the two triangle pairs; it still emits both, so any order works. |
| 4 | `appendBlockIcon(mesh, block, cx, cy, half, depth)` | `.cpp:101-235` | **The big one.** Draws an item as: an isometric 3-face cube; *or* a flat billboard for plants; *or* per-box geometry for model-shaped blocks. | Per-box depth offset `kBoxStep = 0.00002f` by the box's centre-coordinate sum, so nearer boxes sort later. Its comment still says "the depth test" — the mechanism is now the painter's sort (§1.1.7 rule 4). |
| 5 | `appendText(mesh, text, leftX, centreY, charHeight, depth, color, shadow=false)` | `.cpp:250` | A string. Returns width. | Left-aligned. ASCII only. No wrap. §1.6. |
| 6 | `textWidth(text, charHeight)` | `.cpp:237` | Pre-measure for centring. | Must use the same `charHeight` as the draw. |
| 7 | `fontAdvance(char)` | `.cpp:35` | One glyph's advance in cell units. | Returns `kDefaultAdvance` for codepoints ≥ 128. |
| 8 | `setFontAdvances(const std::array<std::uint8_t,128>&)` | `.hpp:52` | Installs the measured table. | Called **once**, from `Main.cpp:1859`. Do not call it again. |
| 9 | `appendStack(mesh, stack, const glm::vec2& centre, slotHalf, iconDepth, countDepth)` | `.hpp:104`, `.cpp:320-345` | Icon **plus** the count label when `count > 1`. | Takes a `vec2` centre, not two floats. Icon is drawn at `slotHalf * 0.72`, so the item does not fill its cell. This is the function a slot should call — not `appendBlockIcon` directly. |
| 10 | `appendTooltip(mesh, text, x, y, aspect, depth)` | `.cpp:347-375` | Dark panel + a purple inner rule + the text. | **Clamps itself to the window** using `aspect`, and **flips above the cursor** near the bottom edge. Uses `TextureLayer::White` (`.cpp:368`). Draws at `depth`, `depth − kLayer`, `depth − 2·kLayer`, text at `depth − 3·kLayer` where `kLayer = 0.00005f` — so **reserve 0.0002 of depth headroom below whatever you pass**. |
| 11 | `appendPointer(mesh, x, y, height, depth)` | `.cpp:377-413` | The gamepad arrow: 3 triangles, white, with an outline. | **The tip is exactly at `(x, y)`** — the arrow hangs down-right from it, which is what makes the hit-test and the drawing agree. Outline sits `kOutlineDepth = 0.00004f` behind. |

**What does not exist and would have to be written:** a nine-slice / stretchable panel, a scrollbar, a button with a pressed state, a checkbox or slider, a text field widget (the search box is bespoke, `InventoryScreen.cpp:457-490`), a progress bar (the furnace's is two sprite crops), a hover highlight for ordinary slots, and any kind of layout container.

The *behaviour* is fine (and better than the comment); the comment predates the scissor. | `game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:416-423` | **certain** (documentation) |

What actually works is the descending painter's sort plus `kBoxStep`. Same class of trap as D2. | `game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.cpp:101-235` | **certain** (documentation) |
| **D5** **NEW** | **The loading screen's four untextured quads are ~22 % too dark.** `LoadingScreen.cpp:38, 40-42, 47-48` pass `kHudLayer` with `textured = false`. `appendQuad` then sets uv `(0.5, 0.5)` (`HudPrimitives.cpp:50`), which on the 185×1687 sheet is pixel (92, 843) — inside the smithing panel — and I measured it: **`#C6C6C6`**. Since `outColor = texel.rgb * fragColor.rgb` (`hud.frag:46`), the background, frame, track and fill all come out at 198/255 = **0.776** of their authored colour. Every other untextured quad in the codebase correctly uses `TextureLayer::White` (`Crosshair.cpp:31`, `DebugOverlay.cpp:14`, `Hotbar.cpp:124`, `HudPrimitives.cpp:368,394`, `InventoryScreen.cpp:457,718`). The uv is constant across the quad, so the derivative is zero and mip 0 is sampled — the value is exactly `#C6C6C6`, not a mip average. | `game/src/hud/LoadingScreen.cpp:38-48` | **certain** (state) / **likely** (that it is visible) — **[unconfirmable visually]** |
| **D6** **NEW** | **A UI element built with 6 indices per quad instead of 12 will silently vanish.** Back-face culling is on (`GraphicsPipeline.hpp:48-52`) and the UI pass applies no projection, so winding is decided purely by the sign of the half-extents. Every existing helper emits both windings, so this has never bitten — but nothing enforces it, there is no assert, and it is not written down anywhere except in the index literal itself. | `game/src/hud/HudPrimitives.cpp:58-59` | **certain** (the state) / **likely** (that it will eventually bite) |
| **D7** **NEW** | **The catalogue's clipped mesh is scissored to a rectangle computed from `catalogueListBounds()` regardless of `Kind`** — `Main.cpp:2988` calls the no-argument overload, while `insideCatalogueList` takes a `Kind`. They agree today because only the two catalogue kinds ever fill `clipped`, and the book card's position does not depend on kind. It is a latent disagreement of exactly the shape `toScreen` exists to prevent. | `game/src/Main.cpp:2988` vs `game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:676,684` | **worth checking** |
| **D8** **NEW** | **Slice 4 shipped without its scrollbar and slice 7 without its clear button**, and neither omission is recorded in `GAPS.md` §2 — `INTERFACE.md` §7 lists both as part of a slice marked ✅. The scrollbar's depth is still reserved and unused. See §1.10. | `game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.cpp:35` (the reserved depth) vs `INTERFACE.md:511-515` | **certain** |

#### 1.9.3 What I could not check without running the game

| Question | Why it needs a frame |
|---|---|
| Whether D5 is actually noticeable | it is a 22 % darkening of already-dark colours |
| Whether the scissor rectangle lands on the right pixels | the mesh-units → pixels conversion at `Renderer.cpp:2201-2218` is straightforward, but off-by-one at the edge is invisible in source |
| Whether the clipped bottom catalogue row looks right | it is drawn as a shortened quad *and* scissored; belt and braces, but I cannot see the seam |
| Whether the gamepad pointer feels right at 1.9 units/s | pure feel; the user is the playtester |
| What the two cards actually do at 5:4 | §1.2.4 is arithmetic, not a screenshot |
| Whether any quad is currently winding-culled | D6 is a latent trap, not an observed bug |

### 1.10 `INTERFACE.md`'s nine slices — verified against the code

`INTERFACE.md:500-520` (§7 "The build order") lists nine slices; its status box (`INTERFACE.md:58, 69`) claims **1–5 and 7 built, 6/8/9 not**. I checked each against source rather than taking the claim.

| Slice | Claim | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** Typed text in `Window` | built | **confirmed** | `consumeTypedText()` declared `engine/include/engine/platform/Window.hpp:170`; consumed at `game/src/Main.cpp:3162-3181` |
| **2** Enumerate items and recipes | built | **confirmed** | `catalogueItems` (`InventoryScreen.cpp:538`) walks `allItems()`; per-recipe `category` is what it filters on |
| **3** The second card, static | built | **confirmed** | `kBookPanelMin{0,555}` (`InventoryScreen.cpp:95`), five tabs at `:239-256`, `appendCatalogue` at `:432` |
| **4** Scrolling | built | **confirmed, minus the scrollbar.** The wheel scrolls a row at a time (`Main.cpp:3930-3958`), the tab reset and `catalogueMaxScroll` (`InventoryScreen.cpp:629`) both exist, and the clipped row is cut by a **real scissor** (`Renderer.cpp:2201-2218`). **No scrollbar is drawn** — `InventoryScreen.cpp:35` still reads `// 0.0034 is left free for the scrollbar.` and nothing else in the repo mentions one. | as cited |
| **5** Craftable colouring | built | **confirmed, with four states not six** — `CellState` (`InventoryScreen.cpp:111-136`) and the comment there explains why: three of vanilla's six are groups (slice 9) and the fourth was built and removed |
| **6** Filter toggle | **not built** | **confirmed absent.** Repo-wide grep for `showCraftable`, `craftableOnly`, `filterCraftable`, `"All recipes"`, `"Craftable recipes"` across `game/src/hud/*` and `Main.cpp` returns **nothing**, and `CatalogueState` (`InventoryScreen.hpp:135-166`) has no such flag among its six fields |
| **7** Search tab | built | **confirmed, minus the clear button.** Field, caret, focus rule and beginning-of-word matching all exist (`InventoryScreen.cpp:457-490`, `:538`, `InventoryScreen.hpp:149-152`). §7's *"and the clear button"* has **no implementation** — grep finds nothing |
| **8** Click to fill the grid | **not built** | **confirmed absent.** The catalogue click is creative-only and gives the item straight to the cursor or the inventory (`Main.cpp:3722-3766`); nothing writes `craftSlots` from a recipe. `InventoryScreen.cpp:116` says so explicitly: *"slice 8 fills the grid on the click rather than remembering it"* — written about a feature that does not exist yet |
| **9** Groups | **not built** | **confirmed absent.** No group state anywhere; the only mention is the comment at `InventoryScreen.cpp:113-114` explaining why `CellState` has four members instead of six |

**So the status box is accurate**, with two refinements worth recording: **slice 4 shipped without its scrollbar** and **slice 7 shipped without its clear button**. Both are small, both are invisible in a code grep unless you know to look, and neither is currently logged in `GAPS.md` §2.

`CatalogueState` (`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.hpp:135-166`) is the whole of the catalogue's mutable state, and the caller owns it so that `build()` stays a pure function:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `tab` | `CatalogueTab` | which of the five |
| `scrollRow` | `int` | **whole rows**, never pixels — a fractional offset "would only make the clipped last row ambiguous" |
| `query` | `std::string` | read by the Search tab only |
| `caretVisible` | `bool` | driven by the caller's clock |
| `searchFocused` | `bool` | set by a click on the field, cleared by a click anywhere else |
| `known` | `unordered_set<ItemId>` | the recipe book; **only ever grows** |
| `restrictToKnown` | `bool` | *"An empty book and no book are different things"* |

### 1.11 The one-page cheat sheet for adding a screen

1. Add a `Kind::` value (`InventoryScreen.hpp:29-72`) **and delete the `default:` in `craftSize` first** (G2.4b).
2. Add a panel row to **both** `tools/make-hud-sheet.ps1` **and** `tools/make-reference-hud.ps1`, then re-run both (§1.3.4).
3. Add its sheet offset constant next to the others (`InventoryScreen.cpp:65-75`).
4. Add a row to `layoutFor` (`InventoryScreen.cpp:284-315`) — panel min, craft size, first craft centre, result centre. All in art pixels, origin top-left.
5. If it stores things: `chestSlotCount`, `isContainer`, `chestSlotCentre` (`InventoryScreen.hpp:232-248`, `.cpp:357`).
6. If it needs an odd slot arrangement: `slotsFor` (`.cpp:339`) and `craftSlotCentre` (`.cpp:320`).
7. Add the block to `isInteractive()` (`game/src/world/Block.hpp:2824-2828`) and to the open switch (`Main.cpp:4370-4423`).
8. Decide what `closeScreen` must give back (`Main.cpp:2789-2827`) — and if the slots are a *view* onto a block, **clear them anyway**.
9. Draw it in `build()` (`InventoryScreen.cpp:707-754`) using §1.8's primitives, at a depth from §1.4.6, into the right one of the three meshes (§1.1.5).
10. Do **not** add a 6-index quad (D6), and do **not** use `kHudLayer` for a solid colour (D5).
