### 5.4 Main menu

**Purpose.** The front door. It appears as the first thing after the window opens and the
atlases upload, replacing today's behaviour where `main()` constructs
`World world(kWorldSeed, …)` at `Main.cpp:1896` and captures the cursor at `:1893` before a
single frame is drawn. It also appears after "Save and Quit to Title" (§5.7) and after
"Title Screen" on the death screen (§5.9).

**Background.** Tiled dirt at 32 art px, tinted `{0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 1}` — full-bleed, the
only element in this section that tracks aspect. The block atlas is uploaded before the menu
runs (`Main.cpp:1814`), so the dirt texture is already resident and this costs one quad.

Two ranked upgrades, both optional and neither on the critical path:
*(a)* run the existing sky/atmosphere pass with a slowly panning camera and no chunks — **S**,
looks far better, and risks only whatever the renderer assumes about an empty world;
*(b)* a true 6-face cubemap panorama from `textures/gui/title/background/panorama_0..5.png`
(1024² each) plus `panorama_overlay.png` — **S–M**, needs a cubemap sampler the renderer does
not have.

**Layout** (art px, origin at screen centre, +y down):

```
logo            256 × 64   centred,  top edge at y = −96
version text      8 px     bottom-left, inset 4,4
buttons         200 × 20   centred column, 24 px pitch (20 + 4 gap)
    Play                        centre y = +4
    Options…                    centre y = +28
    How to Play                 centre y = +52
    Quit Game                   centre y = +84      (12 px extra gap — destructive-ish, kept apart)
```

Widest element 256 px → needs aspect ≥ 1.002. At 4:3 (340 art px wide) there are 42 px of
margin each side. The logo shrinks to 176 × 44 below aspect 1.05 so it never touches the
edges; buttons never move.

The logo is `title/minecraft.png` staged into the widened sheet (§5.1.2) as a 256 × 64 rect.
If the developer prefers the game's own wordmark, the same rect is drawn from
`appendTextCentred("VOXEL GAME", 24 px)` and nothing else changes.

**Controls and states.**

| Control | Normal | Hover | Pressed | Disabled | Focused |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Play | `button` | `button_highlighted`, label 255,255,160 | `button_highlighted`, label offset +1 px down | — | + focus ring |
| Options… | as above | as above | as above | — | + ring |
| How to Play | as above | as above | as above | — | + ring |
| Quit Game | as above | as above | as above | — | + ring |

**Data.** Reads: the count of valid worlds under `saves/` (to decide whether Play goes
straight to §5.5 or straight to §5.6 — if there are zero worlds, Play pushes World Create and
skips the empty list), and the version string. Writes: nothing.

**Navigation.** Default focus **Play**. Up/Down wraps. Escape does nothing (see §5.3.2).
`B` does nothing. Quit Game raises the §5.10 confirmation only if a world were open, which it
never is here — so from the title it quits immediately.

**Strings.** `Play` · `Options…` · `How to Play` · `Quit Game` · footer left
`Voxel Game — M<milestone>` · footer right `Not affiliated with Mojang`.

### 5.5 World select

**Purpose.** Choose which world to load, make a new one, or delete one. It appears from
Main menu → Play when at least one world exists. It replaces nothing, because nothing exists:
`WorldStore` is hardwired to one directory and there is no `directory_iterator` anywhere in
`game/src` or `engine/src`.

**Layout.**

```
title        "Select World"      8 px, centred, y = −108
list         220 wide × 36 per row, centred, top y = −92, bottom y = +48
             → 3 rows visible at 255 art px of screen height; scrolls
scrollbar    6 wide, right of the list at +2 px gap, full list height
buttons      two rows of 98 × 20 at 4 px gap, centred, 24 px pitch
    row 1:   [ Play Selected ]  [ Create New World ]     centre y = +62
    row 2:   [ Delete    ]  [ Back ]                     centre y = +86
```

Widest element 220 px (+ 8 for the scrollbar) → needs aspect ≥ 0.893.

**A row, 220 × 36:**

```
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| [icon 32×32] World Name                              12 Aug 26 |   name 8 px, white
|              Survival · Seed 1337 · 4 days                     |   subline 6 px, grey
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

The icon is **`appendBlockIcon(mesh, BlockId::GrassBlock, cx, cy, 16, depth)`** — the
isometric block icon primitive already exists (`HudPrimitives.cpp:100`) and gives every world
a thumbnail for free. Bedrock's real screenshot thumbnails are cut with the rest of the
screenshot machinery (§5.2). Selected row: `button_highlighted` nine-sliced behind it;
hovered but unselected: a `{1,1,1,0.10}` wash; focused: the ring.

**Every control and its states.**

| Control | States | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Row | normal, hovered, selected, selected+hovered, focused | double-click, or Enter/`A` on a focused row = Play |
| Play Selected | normal / hover / press / **disabled when nothing is selected** / focus | |
| Create New World | normal / hover / press / focus | never disabled |
| Delete | normal / hover / press / **disabled when nothing is selected** / focus | destructive red tint, raises §5.10 |
| Back | normal / hover / press / focus | |
| Scrollbar thumb | normal / hovered / dragging | hidden when content fits |

**Data it reads.** For each subdirectory of `executableDirectory()/"saves"` containing a
readable `world.dat` (§5.6.3): display name, seed, game mode, last-played time, in-game days.
Directories without a `world.dat` are listed with the folder name and `Seed unknown` rather
than hidden — silently hiding a save is how a player loses one. Sort by last played,
descending. **Writes:** nothing except deletion, which is the recursive removal of one
world directory and happens only behind §5.10.

**Navigation.** Default focus is the **first row**, or `Create New World` if the list is
empty. Up/Down move within the list and then step out to the button block; Left/Right move
between the two buttons in a row. Escape / `B` = Back. `Delete` key on a focused row raises
the delete confirmation.

**Empty state.** No worlds: the list area draws `You don't have any worlds yet.` centred at
8 px grey, `Play Selected` and `Delete` are disabled, focus starts on `Create New World`.
(In practice the main menu skips straight past this — it is specified because a player can
delete their last world and land here.)

**Strings.** `Select World` · `Play Selected` · `Create New World` · `Delete` · `Back` ·
`You don't have any worlds yet.` · `Seed unknown` · `Survival` · `Creative` ·
`%s · Seed %u · %d days` · `Last played %d %s %d`.

### 5.6 World create

**Purpose.** Turn a name, a seed and a game mode into a directory on disk and start it.
It replaces editing `Main.cpp:171` and recompiling.

**Layout.** One column, 200 wide, centred; labels are 8 px left-aligned 100 px left of
centre, controls are 200 × 20 directly under their label at a 6 px gap.

```
title            "Create New World"     8 px centred, y = −112
World Name       label y = −92,  field y = −80
Seed             label y = −56,  field y = −44        (+ resolved-seed line at y = −31, 6 px grey)
Game Mode        label y = −12,  cycler y = 0
Bonus Chest      label y = +24,  cycler y = +36       (only if the item exists; else omit)
folder line                       6 px grey, y = +52   "Will be saved as: saves\my-world"
buttons          [ Create ] [ Cancel ]  98 × 20, 4 px gap, centred, y = +76
```

Widest element 200 px → aspect ≥ 0.784.

**Controls.**

| Control | Type | States | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| World Name | TextField | normal / focused / **error** (red 1 px outline) | max 32 chars, filter `isWorldNameChar`, default `New World`, auto-suffixed `New World (2)` if taken |
| Seed | TextField | normal / focused | max 32 chars, filter `isSeedChar`, **empty is legal and means random** |
| Game Mode | Cycler | normal / hover / press / focus | `Survival` ⇄ `Creative`; seeded from `settings.creative_mode`, and the chosen value is written back there as "what to suggest next time" |
| Create | Button | normal / hover / press / **disabled while the name is empty or invalid** / focus | |
| Cancel | Button | normal / hover / press / focus | |

#### 5.6.1 The seed, precisely

Seed entry must accept both a number and a phrase, because the reference does and because a
player who types `banana` expects a world rather than an error.

```
uint32_t resolveSeed(std::string_view text):
    if text is empty                       -> random 32 bits from std::random_device
    if text parses fully as a signed 64-bit integer (optional '-', digits only)
                                           -> static_cast<uint32_t>(value)       // low 32 bits
    otherwise                              -> fnv1a32(text)
```

Full-string parse only: `12ab` is a phrase, not `12`. The **resolved numeric seed is drawn
under the field at 6 px grey** the moment the field changes — `Seed: 1337` — so it can be
written down, and so a phrase seed is never mysterious. `Templates` (the reference's seed
presets, `Ore_UI_-_Create_New_World_Screen__Advanced__Tab_Settings_-_Templates_Button_…`) is
cut; we have no curated seeds.

**Flat world, starting map, bonus chest, cheats, and the whole world-rule toggle list are
cut** (§5.2) except any whose system already exists. Of the reference's Advanced tab, the
only rows we could honour today are `Fire spreads`, `TNT explodes`, `Tile drops` and
`Natural regeneration`; none has a settings key, and adding four world rules is a survival-
section decision, not a UI one. **Specify nothing here; leave the tab out.**

#### 5.6.2 The save folder — the naming scheme does not survive, and this is the flag

`WorldStore.cpp:139`:

```cpp
: m_directory(std::move(root) / ("world_" + std::to_string(seed)) / "chunks"), m_seed(seed) {
```

The folder name is **derived entirely from the seed**. Two independent failures follow, and
the first is data loss:

1. **Two worlds on the same seed collide.** Create "Test" on seed 1337, then "Test 2" on
   seed 1337, and the second silently opens the first's chunks, player, chests and furnaces.
   Nothing warns; the header check at `WorldStore.cpp:152-197` compares the seed and *passes*.
   This is not hypothetical — a player experimenting with one seed is the normal case.
2. **A user-supplied name has nowhere to live.** The path cannot carry it, so the name needs
   a metadata file regardless; and if a future session "fixes" this by putting the raw name
   in the path instead, Windows will reject `Con`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`,
   `LPT1`–`LPT9`, anything containing `\ / : * ? " < > |`, and anything ending in a dot or a
   space — and `MAX_PATH` is already tight because `saves/` sits under the build output
   directory.

**Required change.** `WorldStore` stops composing its own path:

```cpp
WorldStore(std::filesystem::path worldDirectory);   // seed is read from world.dat, not the name
```

and the directory name comes from a slug:

```
slug(name): lowercase; every char not in [a-z0-9-_] -> '-'; collapse runs of '-';
            trim leading/trailing '-'; truncate to 32; if empty -> "world";
            if it matches a Windows reserved device name -> prefix "w-";
            while the directory exists -> append "-2", "-3", …
```

The **display name lives in `world.dat`, never in the path**, so arbitrary names — emoji,
Cyrillic, `NUL`, 200 characters, a single space — are all safe by construction. The screen
shows the resolved folder under the buttons (`Will be saved as: saves\my-world`) so the
mapping is never a surprise.

**Migration, and it matters.** `saves/world_1337/` exists on this machine right now and is
the developer's world. On first run of the new code: if `saves/world_1337/` exists and has no
`world.dat`, write one with `name = "World"`, `seed = 1337`, `gameMode` from the current
`settings.creative_mode`, `created`/`lastPlayed` from the directory's write time — and leave
the folder name alone. It appears in the list on the next boot with everything intact.
`CLAUDE.md` bug shape #8 applies: **read the bytes on disk after writing the first one**,
before declaring it done, and do not bump `kChunkFormatVersion` (`WorldStore.cpp:69`, value
4) — nothing about the chunk payload changes and a bump would regenerate every chunk.

#### 5.6.3 `world.dat`

Sits beside `player.dat`, `furnaces.dat`, `chests.dat`, `stowboxes.dat` and `creatures.dat`
at `m_directory.parent_path()`, and follows exactly the style already there — a trivially
copyable POD with a magic and a version, like `SavedPlayer` (`WorldStore.hpp:26-47`):

```cpp
struct SavedWorld {
    char     magic[4];        // 'V','X','W','D'
    uint32_t version;         // kWorldFormatVersion = 1
    uint32_t seed;
    uint8_t  gameMode;        // 0 survival, 1 creative
    uint8_t  padding[3];
    int64_t  createdUnix;
    int64_t  lastPlayedUnix;
    uint64_t ticksPlayed;
    uint8_t  nameLength;      // 0..64
    char     name[64];        // UTF-8, not NUL-terminated
};
static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<SavedWorld>);
```

`ticksPlayed` gives the world list its "4 days" line and costs one increment per tick.
`lastPlayedUnix` is written by `saveEverything`, so it is correct after both Save-and-Quit and
window close.

**Navigation.** Default focus **World Name**, caret at the end of the pre-filled default with
the text selected so typing replaces it. Tab / Down moves Name → Seed → Game Mode → Create →
Cancel. Enter in either text field moves to the next field rather than activating Create
(pressing Enter twice must not create a world by accident). Escape / `B` = Cancel, and raises
no confirmation because nothing has been written yet.

**Strings.** `Create New World` · `World Name` · `Seed` · `Leave blank for a random seed` ·
`Seed: %u` · `Game Mode` · `Survival` · `Creative` ·
`Search for materials, craft, gain levels, health and hunger` ·
`Unlimited resources, free flying and destroy blocks instantly` ·
`Will be saved as: saves\%s` · `Create` · `Cancel` · `That name is already in use.` ·
`A world needs a name.`

### 5.7 Pause menu

**Purpose.** The thing `Escape` should do. Today `Escape` with no container screen open
merely calls `window.setCursorCaptured(false)` (`Main.cpp:3203-3206`) and the game keeps
running behind a free cursor; `Start` on the pad is explicitly commented *"Start does the same
rather than opening a pause menu, because there is not one yet"* (`Main.cpp:3389`). This
screen replaces both, and it is the **first reachable save the game has ever had** — the
current code writes the world only on window close (`Main.cpp:7033-7100`).

**Appears when:** `Escape` or `Start` with the screen stack empty and the player alive.

**Layout.** No panel; buttons float over the dimmed world, exactly as the reference does.

```
dim quad        full screen, {0,0,0,0.55}   — kDim already exists at InventoryScreen.cpp:44
title           "Game Paused"   8 px centred, y = −72
buttons         200 × 20 centred column, 24 px pitch
    Back to Game            y = −40
    Options…                y = −16
    How to Play             y = +8
    Save and Quit to Title  y = +40      (12 px extra gap)
```

Widest element 200 px. **The world keeps rendering behind the dim** — it is the same frame
path as an open inventory, which already dims at `InventoryScreen.cpp:721`.

**Does it actually pause?** **Yes.** We are single-player-only, which puts us permanently on
the working side of Bedrock's *Enable Game Pause* toggle, so the toggle itself is cut and the
behaviour is unconditional. Precisely:

| Stops | Keeps running |
|---|---|
| `updatePlayer` (`Main.cpp:4136`) | chunk streaming and meshing — `world.update(...)` at `:5840`, so the world is ready on resume |
| `drops.update` (`:5979`) | the frame limiter and the renderer |
| `creatures.update` (`:6244`) | music (`musicVolume` bus) |
| `timeOfDay += deltaSeconds / dayLengthSeconds` (`:6545`) | |
| `weather.update` (`:6566`) | |
| furnace smelting (which today explicitly keeps smelting behind a screen — `Main.cpp:2836-2839`) | |
| world sounds | |

Implement it as a single `simDelta = paused ? 0.0f : deltaSeconds` fed to every simulation
call, **not** by early-returning around them — an early return is how one of the seven gets
forgotten (bug shape #14). **And on resume, clamp the first frame's delta**: the wall clock
has advanced by however long the menu was open, and feeding that into the physics step is a
spiral of death. Reuse whatever clamp the existing loop already applies to `deltaSeconds` at
`Main.cpp:3058`; if there is none, this screen is the reason to add one.

**Controls.** All four are plain Buttons with normal / hover / press / focus. None is ever
disabled. `Save and Quit to Title` carries no confirmation — it saves first, so nothing is
lost — but it **does** show a blocking `Saving world…` frame while `saveEverything` runs, so
a large world does not look like a hang.

**Data.** Reads nothing. Writes: `Save and Quit to Title` calls `saveEverything(...)` (the
hoisted `Main.cpp:7033-7100` block: `world.saveAll()`, `savePlayer`, furnaces, chests,
stowboxes, creatures) plus `SavedWorld::lastPlayedUnix` and `ticksPlayed`, then returns
`ExitReason::ToTitle` from `playWorld`.

**Navigation.** Default focus **Back to Game**. Escape / `B` / `Start` all resume — pause is
the one screen where the back gesture is also the primary action, which is correct and matches
the reference. Up/Down wrap.

**Strings.** `Game Paused` · `Back to Game` · `Options…` · `How to Play` ·
`Save and Quit to Title` · `Saving world…`.

#### 5.7.1 How to Play — the page that retires the function keys

A read-only, scrolling, two-column key list pushed from either the main menu or pause. It
exists because 16 undocumented function keys is the actual state of the game, and a page of
text is the cheapest possible answer.

Layout: title at y = −108, then rows of `label` (left column, right-aligned at x = −8) and
`binding` (left-aligned at x = +8), 12 px pitch, inside a scroll region 220 wide from
y = −92 to y = +96. Group headers at 8 px white, rows at 8 px grey.

Groups and content, taken from the real bindings (`Main.cpp:3198-3373`, `:4104-4133`):
**Movement** — Move `W A S D`, Jump `Space`, Sneak `Left Ctrl`, Sprint `Left Shift`,
Fly (creative) `double-tap Space`. **Interaction** — Break `Left Mouse`, Place/Use
`Right Mouse`, Pick hotbar `1`–`9` / wheel, Drop `Q`, Inventory `E`. **Screens** —
Pause `Escape`, Close screen `Escape`. **Debug** — Overlay `F5`, Debug view `F12`,
Spawn hostile `F8`/`F9`, Force weather `V`.

**Everything else on that list is retired by §5.8 and must be deleted from the key path in
the same slice**, or the game will have two owners for tone mapping, shadows, clouds, input
mode, render distance and the frame cap: `F1`/`F2`, `F3`/`F4`, `F6`/`F7`, `F10`, `F11`, `G`,
`C`, `F`. That is bug shape #2 in the making — a widened path leaving the old one live.

**Navigation.** Scroll only. Escape / `B` pops. Default focus is the scroll region.

### 5.8 Settings — tabbed

**Purpose.** Put the 44 parsed keys and the 12 hotkey actions behind a screen. Appears from
Main menu → Options… and from Pause → Options…; the same screen either way, with per-row
availability differing (§5.8.4).

**Layout.**

```
tab strip     across the top, 24 px tall, top edge y = −112
              tab width = min(130, floor((340 − 4) / 5)) = 67 px, 1 px gap
panel         340 wide, from y = −88 to y = +88, nine-sliced from the existing panel art
scroll region inside the panel, inset 6 px; rows are 24 px (control only)
              or 34 px (control + description line)
buttons       [ Reset to Defaults ] [ Done ]  98 × 20, centred, y = +104
```

Widest element 340 px = 2.663 screen units → **needs aspect ≥ 1.332**. At 4:3 (aspect 1.333)
it exactly fits; below that the panel narrows to `min(340, screenWidthPx − 16)` and the
200 px controls narrow with it down to a 120 px floor. State this in the code, and put a
`static_assert` on the floor: `GAPS.md §2.4` records the existing cards silently running off
both edges below 1.28:1, and this is the same trap.

**A row, Ore-UI-shaped:**

```
 Render Distance                                  [========|=========]   ← slider, right, 200 × 20
 How far the world is drawn                                              ← 6 px grey description
```

Label 8 px white at the row's left inset; description 6 px grey directly under it; control
right-aligned. Where the control is a slider its label carries the value —
`Render Distance: 12 chunks` — because that is the only place a slider's number can live at
this size. Where it is a cycler, the button *is* `Bloom: On`. Group headers (`Performance`,
`Quality`, `Atmosphere`, `Water`) are 8 px white on their own 20 px row with a 1 px
`{1,1,1,0.15}` rule under them, matching the reference's `GENERAL` / `GRAPHICS, PERFORMANCE
AND LAYOUT` bands.

#### 5.8.1 The five tabs, and the rule that keeps them honest

**Video · Audio · Controls · Game · Accessibility.**

**Every option belongs to exactly one tab, always.** Cross-listing an option on two tabs is
bug shape #1 wearing a UI hat — two places to change one value, and one of them will drift.
Enforce it in code: one `constexpr` array

```cpp
struct OptionRow { std::string_view key, label, description; Tab tab; Widget kind; /* range, step, live */ };
constexpr OptionRow kOptions[] = { … };
```

with a `static_assert` that `std::size(kOptions)` equals the number of keys `Settings.cpp`
parses, and a startup probe (the pattern `CLAUDE.md` box item 6 describes) asserting that
every key string in `kOptions` round-trips through `loadSettings`/`saveSettings`. That assert
is the difference between this screen being right and this screen looking right.

#### 5.8.2 Every option — the full table

Ranges and clamps are read from `core/Settings.cpp:119-252` and `core/Settings.hpp`; nothing
below is invented. **Config-only** = reachable today only by editing `settings.cfg`.
**Hotkey** = also reachable today by an undocumented key. **Restart** = takes effect only on
relaunch. **Live** = applies immediately.

`exposure`, `controller_rumble`, `particles` and `foliage_sway` live **here and nowhere
else** — brightness, rumble-off, motion-reduction and flashing-reduction are the four
accessibility levers we actually have, and putting them on Video/Controls instead would leave
the Accessibility tab empty of anything that matters. `GAPS.md` G2.15 asks for text size,
high contrast, text-background opacity and subtitles; none has a system behind it and all four
stay out.

**Hidden — 4 keys that must never appear on any tab**

`worldgen_probe`, `block_probe`, `creature_showcase`, `drop_showcase`. All four are
development probes that exit without opening a window or spawn debug content;
`GAPS.md §2.2` names the first two explicitly. **But the screen must still preserve them.**
`saveSettings` (`Settings.cpp:257`) truncates and rewrites the entire file, so a screen that
builds a fresh `Settings` and saves it would silently wipe every hidden key. Rule: the screen
mutates the **loaded** `Settings` struct in place and passes that same struct to
`saveSettings`. Worth an explicit test.

**Accounting:** 22 + 2 + 5 + 7 + 4 = 40 visible existing keys, plus 4 hidden = **44**, which
is exactly what `Settings.cpp` parses. Plus **3 new keys** (`fov`, `gui_scale`,
`immediate_respawn`) that the screens require and the file does not yet have; `seed` and the
per-world game mode move to `world.dat` (§5.6.3) rather than becoming settings keys.

#### 5.8.3 Which rows are live, and the two that are not

- **Restart:** `worker_threads` only. `JobSystem` is sized once at `Main.cpp:996` and
  `Settings.hpp:24-28` says resizing a live pool "buys a whole class of bugs for nothing".
  Its row shows `Restart required` in `{1, 0.67, 0.25, 1}` under the slider **once changed**,
  and the Done button's tooltip repeats it. A settings screen that silently lied about this
  would be worse than no screen.
- **Next world load:** `start_weather`, `spawn_x`, `spawn_z`, `spawn_underground`.
- **Game Mode** is the one genuinely awkward row, because after §5.6 a mode is a property of
  a *world*, not of the program. Resolution, with one owner each: `settings.creative_mode`
  owns **"what the create screen should suggest next time"**, `SavedWorld::gameMode` owns
  **"what this world is"**. So the row is labelled `Default Game Mode` when the screen is
  reached from the main menu (writes `settings.cfg`) and `Game Mode` when reached from pause
  (writes `world.dat` and takes effect immediately). Same row, two owners, never both at once
  — and the label change is what makes that visible to the player.
- Everything else is live: write the field, call `saveSettings` immediately, and push the
  value into the renderer through the same calls `Main.cpp:2110-2124` already uses.
  **Save on every change, not on Done** — five of the six saving hotkeys already do exactly
  that, and matching them is one fewer behaviour to remember.

#### 5.8.4 Availability from the main menu

Reached without a world, the Game tab's `Game Mode` becomes `Default Game Mode` and rows 6–8
(spawn) are disabled with the note `Applies when a world is loaded.` Everything else is
identical. Nothing is hidden — a disabled row with a reason is better than a tab whose
contents change shape depending on where you came from.

**Navigation.** Default focus is the **first row of the current tab**; the current tab
persists for the session (not to disk). `LB`/`RB` and `PageUp`/`PageDown` change tab.
`Left`/`Right` adjust the focused row. `Escape`/`B`/`Done` pop. `Reset to Defaults` raises
§5.10 (`Reset all settings?` / `Every option returns to its default. This cannot be undone.`)
and resets **only the current tab's** rows, which is both safer and what the label should
then say: `Reset This Tab`.

**Strings.** `Options` · tab names `Video` `Audio` `Controls` `Game` `Accessibility` ·
group headers `Performance` `Quality` `Atmosphere` `Water` · `Done` · `Reset This Tab` ·
`Restart required` · `Applies when a world is loaded.` · `Applies to new worlds.` ·
`Rebinding is not available yet.` · `On` · `Off` · `Auto` · `Unlimited` · `Still` ·
`Main thread only` · `%d chunks` · `%d%%` · `%.2f×` · `%d°`.

### 5.9 Death screen

**Purpose.** Replace the silent 1.6-second teleport. Today `player.deathSeconds` accumulates
(`world/Player.cpp:163-164`), and at `kRespawnSeconds = 1.6f` (`world/Survival.hpp:142`) the
code at `Main.cpp:4284-4322` spills the inventory, closes any screen, picks a bed or the world
spawn, and calls `respawnPlayer`. The player sees a rumble and, if the bed was gone, a console
line they cannot read. Nothing is drawn.

**Appears when:** `!player.alive()` and `player.deathSeconds >= kRespawnSeconds`. **Keep the
1.6 s** — it becomes the "settle the body" beat *before* the screen rather than instead of it,
which is what `GAPS.md` G2.3 asks for. If `immediate_respawn` is on (§5.8.2, Game row 5) the
screen is skipped entirely and today's behaviour is preserved exactly.

**Layout.**

```
dim quad     full screen, {0.40, 0.02, 0.02, 0.55}   — red, distinguishable from the
                                                       neutral {0,0,0,0.55} of every other screen
title        "You Died!"     24 px, centred, y = −56
cause        one line        8 px grey, centred, y = −32, wrapped to 220 px
note         optional        8 px, {1, 0.67, 0.25, 1}, centred, y = −16
buttons      200 × 20 centred column, 24 px pitch
    Respawn                  y = +16
    Title Screen             y = +40
```

The hotbar and status bars **stay hidden** (they already are, `Main.cpp:2966`); the world keeps
rendering behind the tint, unmoving, because the simulation is paused exactly as in §5.7 —
one code path, not two.

**Controls.** `Respawn` and `Title Screen`, both plain Buttons, never disabled.
**Default focus `Respawn`.** Escape and `B` do **nothing** — there is no "back" from being
dead, and popping to a live world would be a bug. `Enter`/`A` on the default focus reproduces
the current one-keystroke feel.

**Data it reads.** `player.deathSeconds`, the resolved respawn point, and one new field:
**the cause.** This is the only new gameplay data any screen in this section needs. Add
`Player::lastDamage` (a `DamageSource` already implied by `world/Survival.hpp`) set wherever
health is reduced, and **one table mapping source → string, in one place** — a `default:`
that returns a generic line is bug shape #10, so the table must be exhaustive with a
`static_assert` on its size against the enum count.

Strings, one per source we actually have: `You died.` · `You fell from a high place.` ·
`You drowned.` · `You burned to death.` · `You went up in flames.` · `You starved to death.` ·
`You suffocated in a wall.` · `You were blown up.` · `You were slain by a %s.` ·
`You were pricked to death.` · `You hit the ground too hard.`

**Data it writes.** Nothing on open. `Respawn` runs today's `Main.cpp:4303-4317` path
unchanged (bed if `hasRespawnPoint` and still a bed, else `spawn_x`/`spawn_z`) and, when the
bed is gone, shows the note **`Your bed was missing or blocked.`** on this screen instead of
the console. `Title Screen` calls `saveEverything` and returns `ExitReason::ToTitle`.

**One timing decision that must be made deliberately.** The inventory is currently spilled as
drops at the 1.6 s mark. Once the screen can be held open indefinitely, spilling on *respawn*
would let a player sit on the death screen and extend the drops' despawn timer arbitrarily.
**Spill at the moment health reaches zero**, as Bedrock does, and keep the 1.6 s purely as a
display delay. That moves three lines from `Main.cpp:4290-4299` earlier and is the whole
change.

### 5.10 The confirmation dialog pattern

**Purpose.** One reusable modal for every irreversible action. Used by: Delete World (§5.5),
Reset This Tab (§5.8), Quit Game from the title if a save is in flight, and Overwrite an
existing world name (§5.6).

**Appears as:** a `ScreenId::Confirm` pushed on top of whatever raised it, at the next stack
depth (§5.3.2), so the screen underneath still draws and receives nothing.

**Layout**, modelled directly on
`Ore_UI_-_Edit_World_Screen__General__Tab_Settings_-_Delete_World_Button_Pop-Ups_(Bedrock).png`:

```
scrim        full screen over the parent, {0,0,0,0.40}
panel        250 wide × (28 + 12·bodyLines + 24·buttonCount + 8) tall, centred
title bar    28 px tall, title 8 px centred; 14 × 14 cross button at the top-right, inset 7 px
body         wrapText(message, 234 px, 8 px), 12 px line pitch, left-aligned, inset 8 px
buttons      200 × 20 stacked, 4 px gap, centred, bottom inset 8 px
    [ safe action ]        ← first, and focused
    [ destructive action ] ← second, red tint {0.85, 0.25, 0.25, 1}
```

Widest element 250 px → aspect ≥ 0.979.

**The safety rules, and they are the point of having a pattern:**

1. **The safe button is first and holds default focus.** Never the destructive one.
2. **Escape, `B` and the cross button all mean *cancel*** — never *confirm*, never *nothing*.
3. **The destructive button is the only red thing on screen.** Red means "this deletes
   something", everywhere, or it means nothing.
4. Clicking the scrim does **not** dismiss — too easy to do by accident with a pad pointer.
5. The dialog owns no state; it takes `{title, message, safeLabel, destructiveLabel}` and a
   callback, and pops itself before invoking it.

**States.** Both buttons: normal / hover / press / focus. Cross button: normal /
`cross_button_highlighted`. Nothing is ever disabled — a dialog with a disabled button is a
dialog that should not have opened.

**Navigation.** Up/Down or Left/Right move between exactly two buttons; `Enter`/`A`
activates the focused one. There is no keyboard shortcut for the destructive button.

**Instances, with their exact wording:**

| Raised by | Title | Message | Safe | Destructive |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delete (§5.5) | `Are you sure?` | `If you delete "%s" it will be gone forever.` | `Cancel` | `Delete World` |
| Reset This Tab (§5.8) | `Reset these options?` | `Every option on this tab returns to its default. This cannot be undone.` | `Cancel` | `Reset` |
| Name in use (§5.6) | `That name is taken` | `A world called "%s" already exists. Create another one anyway?` | `Cancel` | `Create Anyway` |
| Quit while saving | `Quit now?` | `The world is still saving. Quitting now may lose recent changes.` | `Wait` | `Quit Anyway` |

## 6. The HUD we do not have

**Scope:** everything drawn while the player is in the world and *not* in a container
screen, plus how an item is presented anywhere it appears — hotbar, container grid,
dropped entity, thrown entity. Out-of-world menus (main, pause, settings, death, chat)
belong to another fragment and are not repeated here. Overworld only.

**Headline:** the three bars we have are correct and the fourth and fifth do not exist.
The larger hole is not a bar — it is that **an item is drawn in four places and none of
them shows a single thing about its condition.** `ItemStack::damage` has been tracked
since M-whenever, is written by two call sites (`Main.cpp:4791`, `Main.cpp:5248`), is
persisted, and is drawn by nothing. A worn pickaxe and a new one are the same picture
until one of them vanishes. Second-largest: **24 status effects run with no on-screen
trace at all**, and that one is not blocked on anything.

Three things below are blocked on systems that do not exist (experience, armour,
enchanting), one is blocked on there being no boss, and one on there being no
advancements. Everything else can be built today.

---

### 6.1 The unit system, and the one constant everything must derive from

Read this first; every number in the rest of the fragment is expressed in it.

**The convention** (`hud/DebugOverlay.cpp:16-18`, `hud/Hotbar.hpp:21`): screen space is
relative to **window height**. Y runs **−1 at the top to +1 at the bottom**; X runs
**−aspect to +aspect**. The renderer applies the aspect correction, so a width and a
height written in these units are already the same physical size.

**Depth is legacy and inert in the UI pass.** `engine/shaders/hud.frag:3-10` states it
outright: *"The UI pass has no depth attachment at all now, and order alone decides what
covers what."* Every `depth` argument in `HudPrimitives` still exists and still travels
into the vertex, and nothing tests it. **What decides occlusion is the order of the
appends inside a mesh, and then which of the three meshes it went into** — `hud`,
`clipped`, `topLayer` (`Main.cpp:2984-2987`). Anything below that says "drawn behind"
means "appended earlier", not "given a larger depth". Keep passing the existing bands so
the file stays self-consistent, but do not reason with them.

**The reference-pixel constant.** `StatusBars.cpp:52` already establishes the bridge
between the reference's GUI pixels and our units, and it is the single most useful number
in the HUD:

```
kPerReferencePixel = kHotbarWidth / 182.0f
                   = (0.152f * 9) / 182.0f
                   = 0.0075164835f          // one reference GUI pixel, in window-height units
```

Consequences worth writing down once, because six sections below depend on them:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| 1 reference px | 0.0075165 units |
| Screen height (2.0 units) | **266.1 reference px** |
| Screen width at 16:9 (3.5556 units) | 473.0 reference px |
| `kHotbarWidth` | 1.368 units = **exactly 182 reference px** |
| `kHotbarHalfWidth` | 0.684 units = 91 px |
| `kHotbarTopY` | 0.812 |
| 5 px / 8 px / 9 px / 10 px | 0.0375824 / 0.0601319 / 0.0676484 / 0.0751648 |
| 13 px / 16 px / 18 px / 24 px / 25 px | 0.0977143 / 0.1202637 / 0.1352967 / 0.1803956 / 0.1879121 |

**The hotbar, the XP bar and the boss bar are all 182 reference px wide in the reference,
and `kHotbarWidth` is already exactly that.** So all three are the same width here by
construction, and none of them needs a second width constant. That is the whole reason
`StatusBars.cpp` anchors to `kHotbarWidth` and it must not be undone.

Also worth stating plainly: 266 reference px of screen height means **our HUD is 1.35×
larger than Java's default** (360 virtual px at guiScale 3 on a 1080p display). That is a
deliberate-looking choice nobody has ever written down; §6.13 makes it a setting.

**Where the art comes from.** `assets/textures/hud.png` is 185 × 1687 today
(`HudPrimitives.hpp:22`, and `Main.cpp` validates the PNG header against it, which is what
catches the whole sheet drifting). It is written by `tools/make-hud-sheet.ps1` and the
reference's real crops are laid over it into `hud-reference.png` beside the exe by
`tools/make-reference-hud.ps1`, which the game prefers when it exists. **Any new sprite
means one new block in both scripts and one new offset constant in code**, exactly as the
ten status icons at `kStripTop = 1345` already do — the last two of them, absorption's gold
hearts, went in that way on 2026-08-18. **The sheet is only 185 px wide**;
anything wider than that has to be laid out as a grid, and §6.4 does.

**What is not there and cannot be worked around:** there is no post-process hook for the
UI. `hud.frag` samples a sheet, tints it, and stops. Its only per-frame uniform is
`frame.animation` (two layer redirections). Screen overlays that are a *tint* (§6.7) are
therefore HUD quads; screen overlays that are a *distortion* (nausea) must go into
`tonemap.frag`, which is the only pass that writes to the screen.

### 6.2 The experience bar and the level number — **blocked on there being no XP system**

**What Bedrock does.** The experience bar is a **182 × 5** strip centred directly above
the hotbar, drawn as an empty track with a filled progress overlay clipped from the left.
Both sprites exist locally and I measured them:
`gui/sprites/hud/experience_bar_background.png` and `experience_bar_progress.png`, both
**182 × 5**. Sampled at x = 90, the track's five rows are
`#09100C / #202B25 / #28332D / #202B25 / #09100C` and the progress bar's are
`#081C11 / #203A0D / #2E4B15 / #20380D / #081C11` — a dark green with a lit second row,
not a flat fill. The **level number** is drawn centred on the bar in
**`#80FF20`** with a **1-px black outline drawn on all four sides** (not a drop shadow —
the string is drawn five times), sitting so its bottom two rows overlap the bar's top
edge. In Java's geometry the bar's top is 29 px above the screen bottom and the number's
top is 35 px above it. In Bedrock, the whole assembly is identical under the **Classic**
UI profile; under **Pocket** the bars move to the screen corners.
[https://minecraft.wiki/w/Heads-up_display] · sprite sizes measured locally from
`reference\minecraft-assets-26.2\...\gui\sprites\hud\`.

**What we have.** Nothing. `item/Recipe.hpp`'s `repairResult` doc comment (line 116 as of 2026-08-19; the `:123` this replaced was past the end of a 120-line file) says it outright: recipes that *"depend
on enchantments or experience — neither of which exists here"*. Grep across `game/src`
and `engine/` for `experience`, `xp`, `xpLevel`, `ExperienceOrb` finds no field on
`Player`, no orb entity, no smelting reward, no mob drop. The only traces are two sound
events — `SoundEvent::Orb` and `SoundEvent::LevelUp` (`core/Sounds.cpp:23,25`) — both
staged, both loaded, and `LevelUp` is one of the sixteen that no call site ever plays
(`GAPS.md` G9.1). `GAPS.md` G7.2 ranks the system itself **XL · P0**.

**What must be built (the HUD half only).**

1. Two new sprites on the sheet, 182 × 5 each, stacked: one track, one progress. They are
   wider than the sheet's 185 only by three pixels of margin, so they fit as-is.
2. Insert an **XP band** into the vertical stack above the hotbar. The band is 5 px of bar
   plus a 2 px gap:
   ```
   kXpBarHalfWidth  = kHotbarHalfWidth                       // 0.684, i.e. 91 px, free
   kXpBarHalfHeight = 2.5f * kPerReferencePixel              // 0.0187912
   kXpBarBottomY    = kHotbarTopY - 2.0f * kPerReferencePixel// 0.796967
   kXpBarCentreY    = kXpBarBottomY - kXpBarHalfHeight       // 0.778176
   kXpBarTopY       = kXpBarCentreY - kXpBarHalfHeight       // 0.759385
   ```
3. **The progress overlay is a clipped sprite, not a scaled one.** Draw the track full
   width, then draw the progress sprite with both its on-screen half-width *and* its
   source pixel width multiplied by `progress`, left-anchored — `appendSprite` already
   takes an independent `pixelMin`/`pixelSize`, so this needs no new primitive. Scaling
   the whole 182 px into a shorter quad squashes the artwork and is the obvious wrong
   thing.
4. **The level number** at `charHeight = 8 * kPerReferencePixel = 0.0601319`, centred via
   `centreX - textWidth(label, charHeight) * 0.5f`, centre Y at
   `kXpBarTopY - 2 * kPerReferencePixel = 0.744352`. The outline is five `appendText`
   calls: four at ±1 texel in `{0,0,0,1}` then one at `{0.502f, 1.0f, 0.125f, 1.0f}`
   (= `#80FF20`). **`appendText`'s `shadow` flag is not this** — a shadow is one offset
   copy at quarter tint and reads as a drop shadow, where the reference's level number is
   outlined so it stays legible over a bright bar. Add
   `appendOutlinedText(...)` next to `appendText` rather than open-coding it, because
   §6.6 and §6.12 want the same thing.
5. **Push the status rows up.** `kHealthRowY` currently derives from `kHotbarTopY`
   directly (`StatusBars.cpp:64`). It must instead derive from a single
   `kStatusStackTopY` that is the XP bar's top when the bar is shown and the hotbar's top
   when it is not, or the hearts will sit on top of the bar. With the band inserted:
   health/hunger row centre **0.718044**, armour/air row centre **0.642879**. The three
   existing `static_assert`s in `StatusBars.cpp:74-84` must be re-pointed at the new base;
   they are the only thing that will catch this going wrong, because a row overlapping a
   bar by two pixels looks merely *slightly* wrong and nobody can name it.
6. **Hidden in creative**, along with every other bar — already the behaviour at
   `Main.cpp:2958`.

**What the HUD needs from the system, in one line.** `int level` and
`float progress` in `[0,1]` on `StatusValues`. Nothing else — not total XP, not the
per-level cost curve. And per `StatusBars.hpp:52-63`, the rebuild trigger must compare
**the two drawn values**, not a derived total, or the bar will be a frame late.

**Depends on:** an experience system (`GAPS.md` G7.2, XL, P0 — not ours).
**Effort (HUD half): S · Priority: P2** (it cannot be P1 while it draws nothing).

### 6.3 The armour bar — **unblocked 2026-08-19; the only unbuilt half is this one**

**What Bedrock does.** Ten **9 × 9** icons on an **8 px pitch**, left-aligned exactly like
the hearts, one 10 px row **above** the health row — i.e. the mirror position of the
bubble row, which sits above hunger on the right. Three sprites, all present locally at
9 × 9: `hud/armor_empty.png`, `hud/armor_half.png`, `hud/armor_full.png`. The row is
**hidden entirely when armour points are zero**, and hidden in creative. Twenty points of
armour = ten full icons, counted in halves exactly as health is.
[https://minecraft.wiki/w/Heads-up_display] · sprite sizes measured locally.

**What we have.** ⚠️ **Rewritten 2026-08-19 09:57 — this paragraph said the opposite and would have
sent a reader to build the wrong half.** *Was: "The data and none of the behaviour… `armourDefence`
and `armourToughness` are referenced only at their own definitions. There are no armour slots on
`Inventory`, no damage reduction, no `Region::Armour` wiring."* **All of that is now false.**
`item/Item.hpp` carries `ArmourSlot`, `isArmour`, `armourSlot`, `armourMaterial`,

`{3,8,6,3}` diamond, `{3,8,6,3}` Emberite, turtle helmet 2) and `armourToughness` — **and both are
read for real**: `Inventory` has four equipment slots and `armourSet()` sums them,
`InventoryScreen.cpp` `slotAt` produces `SlotHit{Region::Armour, i}` and `build` draws the column,
`Survival.hpp` `armourDamageTaken` reduces the blow, `Main.cpp`'s `hurtPlayer` reaches it from every
combat path, and the worn set is saved at player format v7. **So the number this bar needs already
exists and is non-zero in play** — `inventory.armourSet().defence`, capped at 20 = ten icons.
**Nothing outside this document blocks it any more.** `GAPS.md` G2.4's armour half is closed; only its
offhand half remains.

**What must be built (the HUD half only).**

1. Three sprites appended to the existing status strip. **The strip is currently ten
   icons and its order is load-bearing in three places** — `New-StatusStrip` in
   `tools/make-hud-sheet.ps1`, the `$statusFiles` array in `tools/make-reference-hud.ps1`,

   ArmourHalf` at the end of all three (never insert into the middle — absorption's gold
   pair was appended that way on 2026-08-18) and the strip becomes thirteen icons at the

2. One more call to the existing `appendHalvesRow`, with `emptyIcon/fullIcon/halfIcon`

### 6.4 Status effect icons — **not blocked, and the best value in this fragment**

**What Bedrock does.** Every effect the player has is shown **top-right**. From the wiki
page: *"Effects that run out sooner appear farther to the left, and effects that are about
to run out start to flash. Additionally, positive effects are shown on the top, and other
effects (neutral or negative) are shown on the bottom. Beacon effects have a blue (instead
of gray) outline."* [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Heads-up_display]

Measured locally, the art is exact:

- `gui/sprites/hud/effect_background.png` — **24 × 24**, the grey frame.
- `gui/sprites/hud/effect_background_ambient.png` — **24 × 24**, the blue (beacon) frame.
- `textures/mob_effect/*.png` — **18 × 18** each, **39 files present**, including every
  one of ours: `speed`, `slowness`, `haste`, `mining_fatigue`, `strength`,
  `instant_health`, `instant_damage`, `jump_boost`, `nausea`, `regeneration`,
  `resistance`, `fire_resistance`, `water_breathing`, `invisibility`, `blindness`,
  `night_vision`, `hunger`, `weakness`, `poison`, `wither`, `health_boost`, `absorption`,
  `saturation`, `slow_falling`.

Layout: frames on a **25 px horizontal pitch** from the right edge, 1 px clear of it; the
beneficial row 1 px from the top, the harmful row **26 px** below it; the 18 × 18 icon
centred in its 24 × 24 frame (3 px inset). Bedrock additionally prints the **remaining
time under the icon** as `M:SS` — that part is observed behaviour, not a pixel-sourced
number, and is flagged as such below.

**What we have.** The whole simulation and nothing on screen. `world/Effects.hpp`:
`enum class Effect : std::uint8_t` (:15) using **Bedrock's own effect ids**, so the values
are *not* contiguous — 24 and 25 are skipped and `Count = 27`, giving **24 real effects,
not 26**. `struct EffectInfo { const char* name; bool harmful; std::uint32_t colour; bool
instant; }` (:46) and the `constexpr effectInfo()` table (:59-108) already carry **the
display name and the harmful flag** — which are precisely the two things this feature
needs and would otherwise be written down a second time. `ActiveEffect { Effect id; int
amplifier; float secondsLeft; }` (:111), `kMaxActive = 8` (:120), and
`Effects::all()`/`count()` are both `constexpr` accessors (:212, :214).
`Player::effects` at `Player.hpp:174`, ticked at `Player.cpp:286-299`, applied at
`Main.cpp:4886/4891/6006/6009`, cleared by milk at `Main.cpp:4992`. **No file under
`game/src/hud/` includes `Effects.hpp`.**

**What must be built.**

1. **Sheet layout.** 24 icons at 18 × 18 will not fit in one row of a 185-px-wide sheet.
   Lay them out as a **10-column grid on an 18 px pitch — 180 × 54** — plus a **48 × 24**
   two-frame strip (normal, ambient) beneath it. Sheet grows 1687 → **1765**, and
   `kSheetSize` in `HudPrimitives.hpp:22` must follow it or every sprite in the game
   silently skews.
2. **`constexpr int effectIconIndex(Effect)`** mapping the sparse Bedrock ids onto the
   dense grid. **No `default:` returning a real value** — bug shape #10; make it a switch
   over every enumerator so a new effect fails to compile rather than drawing `Speed`.
   Add `static_assert(effectIconIndex(Effect::SlowFalling) == 23)` and one for
   `Effect::Speed == 0` so the grid and the table can never drift.
3. **`makeEffectIcons(const effects::Effects&, float aspect)`**, a pure function of a
   snapshot in the same shape as `makeStatusBars`. Layout:
   ```
   frameHalf   = 12 * kPerReferencePixel   // 0.0901978
   iconHalf    =  9 * kPerReferencePixel   // 0.0676484
   pitch       = 25 * kPerReferencePixel   // 0.1879121
   rowGap      = 26 * kPerReferencePixel   // 0.1954286
   rightEdge   = aspect - 1 * kPerReferencePixel
   row0CentreY = -1.0f + (1 + 12) * kPerReferencePixel   // -0.902286
   row1CentreY = row0CentreY + rowGap                    // -0.706857
   ```
   Beneficial (`!effectInfo(id).harmful`) on row 0, harmful on row 1; within a row,
   **sorted by `secondsLeft` ascending and laid out right-to-left**, so the one about to
   expire sits leftmost — that is the reference's rule and it is the opposite of the
   obvious "insertion order" implementation.
4. **Duration text** under each icon: `M:SS` (`"%d:%02d"`, and just `SS` under ten
   seconds), `charHeight = 8 * kPerReferencePixel`, white with `shadow = true`, centred on
   the frame, its centre one row (10 px) below the frame's bottom. *Flagged: the format
   and placement are Bedrock behaviour observed rather than a measured sprite. If it
   crowds the icons, drop to a 6 px text height rather than moving it.*
5. **Amplifier**: a roman numeral (`II`, `III`, `IV`) appended to nothing — the reference
   puts it in the *inventory* screen, not the HUD. Do not draw it here.
6. **The expiry flash.** The reference flashes an effect whose remaining time is under
   **10 seconds (200 ticks)**. Implement as an alpha modulation on both the frame and the
   icon: `alpha = secondsLeft >= 10 ? 1.0f : 0.55f + 0.45f * cos(secondsLeft * 12.566f)`
   (≈2 Hz), passed as the tint to `appendSprite`, which already takes one. **The flash
   must not be a visibility toggle** — an icon that disappears for half a second reads as
   the effect having ended.
7. **Instant effects never appear.** `effectInfo().instant` is already true for
   `InstantHealth`/`InstantDamage`; they are applied and gone within a tick, and drawing
   them produces a one-frame flicker. Skip them.
8. **Rebuild trigger.** The panel changes every second (the countdown), so it cannot ride
   `hudDirty`. Follow the `airRow()` pattern (`StatusBars.hpp:52-63`): a small
   `EffectRow`-style struct with `operator==` describing **exactly what is drawn** —
   ids, whole seconds, and the flash phase quantised to the frame — compared against the
   last drawn one. Comparing `effects.count()` leaves the countdown frozen; comparing
   `secondsLeft` as a float rebuilds every frame.
9. **Not hidden in creative.** Effects are equally real in both modes and the reference
   shows them in both.

**Depends on:** nothing. Every input exists and is `constexpr`.
**Effort: M · Priority: P1.** This is the highest-value unblocked item in the fragment:
24 systems that already change how the game plays and currently announce themselves only
by the player noticing they move faster.

### 6.5 Item presentation, everywhere — the biggest single item

This applies to **four draw paths**, and `CLAUDE.md` bug shape #13 is precisely about
forgetting the last two:

| # | Path | Function | File |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hotbar | `makeHotbar` | `hud/Hotbar.cpp:96` |
| 2 | Every container grid + the catalogue + the held stack | `hud::appendStack` | `hud/HudPrimitives.cpp:307` |
| 3 | Dropped item on the ground | `ItemEntities::buildMesh` | `world/ItemEntity.cpp:219` |
| 4 | Thrown item in flight | `Projectiles::buildMesh` | `world/Projectile.cpp:311` |

**A finding that must be fixed before anything else in this section: the icon box has two
owners.** `appendStack` sizes the icon at `slotHalf * 0.72f` (`HudPrimitives.cpp:311`);
`Hotbar.cpp` sizes it at `kHotbarSlotSize * 0.5f * kIconScale` with `kIconScale = 0.56f`
(`Hotbar.cpp:38, 131`). The count label likewise: `slotHalf * 0.84f` in one and a fixed
`kCountHeight = 0.042f` in the other. Today that is invisible, because a count is a small
label in a corner. **The moment a durability bar exists it stops being invisible**, because
the bar is specified as a fraction of a 16-px item box and two different boxes put it in
two different places on the same screen. Give the item box one owner —
`hud::itemBoxHalf(float slotHalf)` — and have both call it. This is bug shape #5.

#### 6.5a Stack count text

**What Bedrock does.** The count is drawn **bottom-right of the 16 × 16 item square**,
right-aligned, in white, **with the standard one-texel drop shadow**. In Java's geometry
it is right-aligned to `x + 17` with its baseline at `y + 9` within an 18-px slot — i.e.
hard against the item's bottom-right corner, overhanging the icon slightly. A count of 1
is not drawn.

**What we have.** Drawn, but in the **bottom-left** corner in both paths
(`Hotbar.cpp:167-171`, `HudPrimitives.cpp:322-325`), **with no shadow**, at two different
sizes. The `count > 1` rule is correct in both.

**Corrected 2026-08-18** — this entry said "top-left", and it is wrong on the vertical.
Screen +Y is **down** in this project, so `centreY + slotHalf - countHeight * 0.5f` is the
**bottom** of the slot and both paths already bottom-aligned. Only the horizontal and the
shadow were ever wrong. Left uncorrected, the next reader moves a correct edge.

**What must be built.** Move both to bottom-right, right-aligned:
`leftX = iconCentreX + iconHalf - textWidth(label, countHeight)`, centre Y
`iconCentreY + iconHalf - countHeight * 0.5f`; pass `shadow = true`. One shared
`hud::appendStackDecorations(mesh, stack, centre, iconHalf, depth)` that draws count, bar
and sweep, called by paths 1 and 2. Text height is **`iconHalf`**: the glyphs are 8 art
pixels tall in a 16-pixel item square, and `iconHalf` is already half of that square.
(This said `iconHalf * 0.5f`, which is half again and draws the count at 4 pixels —
arithmetic corrected 2026-08-18 along with the "top-left" above.)
**Depends on:** nothing. **Effort: XS · Priority: P0.**

#### 6.5b Durability bar

**What Bedrock does.** A **13 × 2** bar inside the 16 × 16 item square at offset
**(2, 13)** from the square's top-left. A solid black `#000000` 13 × 2 background, and
over its **top row only** a 13 × 1 coloured fill of width `round(13 × remaining)`. The
colour is HSV with saturation and value pinned at 1 and **hue = remaining / 3**, so it
runs pure green at full, yellow at half and pure red as it breaks. Drawn only when the
item is damaged at all — a full-durability tool shows no bar.
[https://minecraft.wiki/w/Durability] and the decompiled `ItemRenderer` geometry
(13 × 2 at (2,13), `Math.round(13.0F - damage * 13.0F / maxDamage)`,
`hsvToRgb(max(0, 1 - damage/maxDamage) / 3.0F, 1.0F, 1.0F)`).

**What we have.** Nothing draws it. `ItemStack::damage` (`Item.hpp:1582`) is incremented
at `Main.cpp:4791` and `Main.cpp:5248` and compared against
`toolFor(item).durability` (`item/Tool.hpp:35-44`). **There is no `maxDurability()` free
function** — the two call sites each reach into `ToolProperties`. Grep for
`durabilityBar` / `damageBar` returns nothing.

**What must be built.**

1. **`constexpr int maxDurabilityOf(ItemId)`** in `item/Tool.hpp`, returning
   `toolFor(item).durability` (0 = never wears). One owner; the HUD must not reach into
   `ToolProperties` itself, and neither should the two wear sites.

   **Done differently, 2026-08-18, and the difference matters.** `item/Tool.hpp` has an
   owner who is not the HUD's, so the HUD reads `mining::toolProperties(item).durability`
   from `item/Mining.hpp` instead — which is already `constexpr`, is already the one table
   (`kTools`, 27 rows) and is what `toolFor` itself is one line onto. `maxDurabilityOf` is
   still worth hoisting for the **two wear sites**, and remains open for that owner.
2. Geometry, as fractions of the item box so both draw paths agree:
   ```
   left   = iconCentre.x - iconHalf + iconSize * (2.0f / 16.0f)
   width  =                            iconSize * (13.0f / 16.0f)
   top    = iconCentre.y - iconHalf + iconSize * (13.0f / 16.0f)
   height =                            iconSize * (2.0f / 16.0f)   // black
   fillH  =                            iconSize * (1.0f / 16.0f)   // colour, top row only
   fillW  = width * (std::round(13.0f * remaining) / 13.0f)        // quantised to 13 steps
   ```
   **Quantise the fill to thirteen steps.** A continuously shrinking bar is not what the
   reference does and it makes a 1500-durability tool look like it never moves.
3. **The colour ramp, written as a `constexpr` with its own asserts** rather than calling
   a general HSV routine. For S = V = 1 and hue = `f/3` where `f` is the remaining
   fraction, the whole conversion collapses to two lines:
   ```cpp
   constexpr glm::vec4 durabilityColour(float remaining) {
       const float f = std::clamp(remaining, 0.0f, 1.0f);
       return f <= 0.5f ? glm::vec4{1.0f, 2.0f * f, 0.0f, 1.0f}
                        : glm::vec4{2.0f - 2.0f * f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f};
   }
   static_assert(durabilityColour(1.0f)  == glm::vec4{0, 1, 0, 1});  // full  -> green
   static_assert(durabilityColour(0.5f)  == glm::vec4{1, 1, 0, 1});  // half  -> yellow
   static_assert(durabilityColour(0.0f)  == glm::vec4{1, 0, 0, 1});  // spent -> red
   ```
   `CLAUDE.md` bug shape #9 is exactly this: *"a standard formula written from memory can
   come out inverted"*. Three compile-time points is the whole defence, and both sides are
   `constexpr`, so it can never rot.

   **Corrected 2026-08-18:** `glm::vec4`'s `operator==` is not usable in a constant
   expression on every GLM version, so these three asserts as written do not compile.
   `HudPrimitives.cpp` splits the ramp into `durabilityRed` / `durabilityGreen` scalars
   and asserts those at the same three points. An assert that cannot be written is an
   assert that does not exist.
5. **Show only when `damage > 0 && maxDurability > 0`.** The durability gate is not
   redundant: **`ItemStack::damage` is overloaded**, and on a *stowbox* it names which
   contents the box is carrying rather than wear (`Item.hpp:1645-1648`). A box holding
   one thing has `damage == 1`, and gating on damage alone grows it a red bar.
4. Draw with `appendQuad(..., TextureLayer::White, false)` — flat colour, no sprite, no
   sheet row needed.
6. **Paths 3 and 4 (the ground drop and the thrown item) get no bar.** The reference draws
   none either; a 13 × 2 strip on a billboarded sprite in the world is unreadable. Say so
   in the comment so nobody adds it later thinking it was missed.

**Depends on:** nothing. **Effort: S · Priority: P0.**

#### 6.5c The hover tooltip

**What Bedrock does.** A dark panel with a **gradient violet border**, offset down-right
of the cursor, flipping and clamping at the screen edges. The nine-slice art is present
locally and I read the exact colours out of it:

- `gui/sprites/tooltip/background.png` — 100 × 100, `.mcmeta` says
  `nine_slice, border: 9`. **Every interior pixel is ARGB `#F0100010`** — a near-black
  violet at 94 % alpha.
- `gui/sprites/tooltip/frame.png` — 100 × 100, `.mcmeta` says
  `nine_slice, border: 10, stretch_inner: true`. The frame is a **one-pixel rule at inset
  9** and it is a **vertical gradient**: ARGB `#505000FF` at the top edge fading to
  `#5028007F` at the bottom (I scanned every non-transparent pixel; those are the two
  endpoints and the 130-odd values between them are a linear ramp). Alpha is a constant
  0x50 = 80/255 = **31 %**.

Content, Bedrock: the **item name**, plus enchantment lines when enchanted, plus (in the
hotbar name popup) the contents of a shulker box. The name line is white; enchantment
lines are a dimmer accent colour.

**What we have.** `hud::appendTooltip` (`HudPrimitives.cpp:329-375`) — and it is better
than it sounds. It already does the offset-down-right, the X clamp to `±aspect` and the
**flip above the cursor** when it would overflow the bottom. It draws three concentric
quads: panel `{0.05, 0.03, 0.09, 0.94}`, edge `{0.32, 0.16, 0.62, 1.0}`, panel again.
That is a solid-colour approximation of the reference's gradient border and **it is
already the right colour family**. Its limits: **one line only**, no wrap, no `\n`, and
the caller passes only `displayNameOf(under->item)` (`InventoryScreen.cpp:831`).

**What must be built.**

1. **Take `std::span<const TooltipLine>` instead of one `string_view`**, where
   `TooltipLine { std::string_view text; glm::vec4 colour; }`. Height becomes
   `lines * charHeight + (lines - 1) * lineGap + 2 * padding` with
   `lineGap = charHeight * 0.25f`; width is the max `textWidth`. Everything else in the
   function is already correct and stays.
2. **Make the border a real gradient.** Two quads instead of one, or — better — one
   `appendQuadCorners` call, which already exists and takes four freely placed corners;
   the vertex colour is per-vertex, so a top-to-bottom ramp from
   `{0.313, 0.0, 1.0, 0.31}` to `{0.157, 0.0, 0.498, 0.31}` is free. Those are
   `#5000FF`/`#28007F` at alpha 0x50, straight off the measured sprite.
3. **Line content, in order:**
   - name — `displayNameOf(item)` (`world/Creature.hpp:786`, **not** `itemDisplayName`,
     which returns "Spawn Egg" for all 56 eggs), white `{0.94, 0.94, 0.98, 1}`.
   - **durability** when damaged: `"Durability: 132 / 250"`, dim
     `{0.62, 0.62, 0.68, 1}`. *Flagged: this line is ours, not Bedrock's — the reference
     shows condition only as the bar. It is cheap, it is what a player actually wants, and
     it costs one line.*
   - shulker/stowbox contents when the stack is one: `damage` doubles as the stowbox
     index (`Item.hpp:1550-1553`), so the contents are reachable. Bedrock does show these.
   - enchantment lines — **blocked**, see 6.5e.
4. **Wire it to the hotbar too**, which is what §6.6 is.

**Depends on:** nothing for the first three. **Effort: S · Priority: P1.**

#### 6.5d Cooldown sweep

**What Bedrock does.** A translucent white overlay covering the **bottom** portion of the
16 × 16 item square, draining downward as the cooldown expires. Java's geometry is exact:
`l = floor(16 * (1 - remaining))`, fill from `y + l` to `y + 16` in **`0x7FFFFFFF`** —
white at 50 % alpha. At the instant of use the whole square is covered; at expiry, none of
it.

**What we have.** Two ad-hoc float timers living as locals inside `main()` and reaching
nothing: `kPearlCooldownSeconds = 1.0f` (`Main.cpp:104`) with `pearlCooldown`
(`Main.cpp:2423`, ticked 4491, tested 5273, set 5296), and `breakCooldown`
(`Main.cpp:2342`). **There is no cooldown concept on `ItemStack` or in the item system**,
and there is no shield (`GAPS.md` G7.10).

**What must be built.** A `float cooldownFor(ItemId)` accessor fed by a small
`std::array<float, N>` of active per-item cooldowns owned beside the inventory, and one
quad in `appendStackDecorations`:
`appendQuad(..., centre.x, top + coveredHalf, iconHalf, coveredHalf, ..., {1,1,1,0.5f},
TextureLayer::White, false)` where `covered = iconSize * remaining` quantised to
sixteenths.
**Depends on:** the cooldowns being promoted out of `main()` locals. **Effort: XS ·
Priority: P2** — with exactly one item that has a cooldown, the payoff today is one
ender pearl.

#### 6.5e Enchantment glint — **blocked on there being no enchanting**

**What Bedrock does.** A scrolling iridescent sheen **masked to the item's own silhouette**
and blended **additively**. The texture exists locally: `textures/misc/enchanted_glint_item.png`
is **128 × 128**, and `enchanted_glint_armor.png` is the armour variant. The reference
draws it as **two layers** of that texture, scaled well past the icon, rotated in opposite
directions (roughly ±10°) and scrolled at different speeds so the two interfere; the
result is multiplied by the item's alpha so it never spills outside the sprite.

**What we have.** Nothing, and nothing to put it on: `item/Recipe.hpp`'s `repairResult` doc comment (line 116 as of 2026-08-19; the `:123` this replaced was past the end of a 120-line file) —
*"neither of which exists here"*. `EnchantingTable` is a block name and
`EnchantedGoldenApple` an item name; there is no enchantment data on `ItemStack`.

**What kind of shader this needs — say it plainly, because it is the reason this is not
cheap.** It cannot be done with the existing primitives. `hud.frag` outputs
`texel.rgb * fragColor.rgb`, one sample, one layer; a second quad laid over the item would
be a **square** of sheen, not a masked one. It needs, in **both** `hud.frag` and the world
path (`gbuffer.frag` / `triangle.frag`, because path 3 and 4 draw items too):

- one new sampler or a reserved layer index for the glint sheet;
- a new `glm::vec4` in `FrameUniforms` carrying the two scroll offsets — and note that
  header's own rule (`FrameUniforms.hpp:17-20`): *"Adding a member means adding it to the
  `Frame` block in every shader that reads it, in the same order"*;
- a per-vertex flag (the existing `layer` float can carry a sentinel, as `kHudLayer` and
  `kFontLayer` already do) selecting the glint branch;
- output `item.rgb + glint0.rgb * item.a + glint1.rgb * item.a`, alpha `item.a`.

The HUD mesh is rebuilt every frame anyway, so **the scroll could be done on the CPU as UV
offsets and no uniform would be needed for path 1 and 2** — but paths 3 and 4 are chunked
world geometry and cannot. Do it once, in the uniform, for all four.

**Depends on:** an enchanting system (absent); `GAPS.md` G9.14 ranks it
**S (shader) / L (mechanic) · P2**.
**Effort: M · Priority: P3.**

---

### 6.6 The hotbar's remaining behaviour

#### 6.6a The item-name popup

**What Bedrock does.** *"When the player switches an item in hand by scroll wheel or 1-9,
its name is shown above the experience level for a short period of time. In Java Edition
this name appears in italics, while in Bedrock Edition, the text has a black background
and also shows enchantments of the selected item, and contents of a shulker box. The
background opacity can be adjusted with the 'Text Background Opacity' option in the
accessibility settings."* [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Heads-up_display]

Java's timing is exact and is the right model: the timer is set to **40 ticks (2.0 s)** on
a switch, the text is fully opaque until the last **10 ticks (0.5 s)**, then fades
linearly — `alpha = min(255, remaining * 256 / 10)`. Centred horizontally; vertically it
sits above the XP bar, and **moves 14 px down when there are no bars** (creative).

The same channel carries Bedrock's **"Identify" / Describe** feature: *"Once pressed
in-game, this shows above the hotbar (as an item tooltip) the name of the block or entity
the player currently faces."* That matters for §6.8 — **Bedrock's answer to "what am I
looking at" is this popup, not a floating name tag.**

**What we have.** The name is written to **the console**: `Main.cpp:4069-4075` logs
`"Holding: …"` on every HUD rebuild, using `displayNameOf`. `GAPS.md` G2.8 ranks it
**XS · P2**. The hotbar selector itself is finished and correct — `kSelectedCell`
(25 × 25 sprite) drawn at `kSelectedScale = 25/21` so the frame overhangs its neighbours
exactly as the artwork intends (`Hotbar.cpp:29-33`), on a nearer band so it is not clipped
by them (`Hotbar.cpp:44-46`). **Do not touch the selector.**

**What must be built.**

1. `float nameFadeSeconds` beside `selectedSlot`, set to **2.0 f** on any change of
   `selectedSlot` **or of the selected slot's item** (picking up a block into the held
   slot should name it too — that is Bedrock's behaviour and it is the case a naive
   "on scroll" implementation misses).
2. `makeHeldItemName(const ItemStack&, float fadeSeconds, bool barsShown)` appending:
   a black panel at `alpha = 0.4f * a`, then the name centred, white, `shadow = true`,
   at `alpha = a`, where
   `a = std::min(1.0f, nameFadeSeconds / 0.5f)`.
   Centre Y: `kXpBarTopY - 10 * kPerReferencePixel` when bars are shown, and
   `+ 14 * kPerReferencePixel` lower when they are not.
   `charHeight = 8 * kPerReferencePixel`. Panel half-width
   `textWidth * 0.5f + 2 * kPerReferencePixel`.
3. **Delete the console line**, or at minimum stop calling it every rebuild — it is the
   only thing that channel is doing and it fires far more often than the name changes.
4. **The rebuild trigger** is a continuous case like the bow draw and the dig bar
   (`Main.cpp:3956-4010`): while `nameFadeSeconds > 0` the HUD must rebuild. Compare the
   **drawn alpha quantised to 1/64**, not the raw float, or it rebuilds every frame for
   two seconds.

**Depends on:** nothing (the fade position wants §6.2's `kXpBarTopY`, but falls back to
`kHotbarTopY` cleanly).
**Effort: XS · Priority: P1.**

#### 6.6b The selector, and one thing genuinely missing from it

The selection frame is done. What is missing is the **attack-cooldown indicator** —
`hud/hotbar_attack_indicator_background.png` and `_progress.png`, both **18 × 18**, plus
the crosshair variants at 16 × 4 and 16 × 16. Bedrock **does not have an attack cooldown**
(that is a Java mechanic), and `CLAUDE.md` names attack cooldown explicitly as a place
where *"Bedrock wins"*. **So: do not build this, and this line exists so nobody has to
work that out again from the sprites being present.**

### 6.7 Damage and state feedback

**Nothing in this section exists**, with two exceptions noted below. `GAPS.md` G9.12 ranks
the lot **M · P1**: *"Burning, drowning, wearing a pumpkin and taking a hit are all
visually identical to standing still."*

**The mechanism, once, for all of them.** There is no post-process hook for the UI. A
*tint* overlay is a full-screen quad appended into the HUD mesh **first, before the
crosshair** (order decides, §6.1) — one `appendQuad` at `centreX = 0, centreY = 0,
halfWidth = aspect, halfHeight = 1.0f`. A *distortion* is not, and must go into
`tonemap.frag`, the only pass that writes to the screen.

#### 6.7a Damage flash and hurt tilt — **the best value here**

- **Bedrock:** a red screen flash on taking damage, and a camera shake with its own
  accessibility toggle. Java instead tilts the view **14°** shaped by `sin(t⁴ · π)` over
  the hurt time. Bedrock wins by project rule, so the flash is the primary and the tilt is
  an option.
- **We have:** `Player::hurtFlash` (`Player.hpp:153`) with `kHurtFlashSeconds = 0.35f`
  (`Survival.hpp:40`), and its **only** consumer is a 0.004-unit heart jitter
  (`StatusBars.cpp:136`).
- **Build:** a full-screen red quad, `{1, 0, 0, 0.30f * (hurtFlash / kHurtFlashSeconds)}`,
  appended first. The value is already on `StatusValues`. Optional tilt behind a
  `camera_shake` setting: `-14° * sin(π * t⁴)` with `t = 1 - hurtFlash/kHurtFlashSeconds`,
  applied to the view matrix. **Peak alpha 0.30, not 0.5** — this fires on every point of
  fall damage and a heavier flash becomes unbearable within a minute of play.
- **Effort: XS · Priority: P1.**

#### 6.7b Low-health heart shake

- **Bedrock/Java:** hearts jitter by **a random 0 or 1 GUI pixel vertically, per heart,
  per tick**, when health is **at or below 4** (two hearts), and separately use the
  `_blinking` sprite variants while the hurt flash runs. **48 heart sprites are present
  locally** in `gui/sprites/hud/heart/` — `full`, `half`, `container` and their
  `_blinking`, `poisoned_`, `withered_`, `frozen_`, `absorbing_` and `hardcore_` variants,
  all 9 × 9.
- **We have:** a jitter, but keyed to the **wrong thing**. `StatusBars.cpp:136` shakes on
  `hurtFlash > 0`, in a fixed alternating `i % 2` pattern, at a fixed 0.004 — which is
  *the hit*, not *low health*. The reference does both, for different reasons: the blink
  says "you were hit", the shake says "you are about to die".
- **Build:** keep the hurt blink (swap in `_blinking` sprites — three more strip entries),
  and add `jitter = health <= 4 ? kPerReferencePixel * random01() : 0.0f` per heart. The
  random needs a per-tick seed so it does not shimmer at frame rate; the reference seeds
  from the tick counter, and that is worth copying exactly.
- **Effort: XS · Priority: P1.**

#### 6.7c Fire overlay

- **Bedrock:** the burning player's view is filled by the fire animation from the bottom,
  ~90 % opaque, leaving the middle of the screen partly readable.
- **We have:** `Player::burningSeconds` and `burnTimer` (`Player.hpp:169-170`), fed and
  ticked, with **no visual consumer at all**. The art is already in the block array:
  `kFireSprite` / `kFireFrameFirst` (`Main.cpp:6890-6893`).
- **Build:** two quads sampling the fire layer — one across the bottom third at full
  height, one narrower — at `alpha 0.9`, appended first, gated on `burningSeconds > 0`.
  Because `hud.frag` already honours `frame.animation`, the flames animate for free.
- **Effort: S · Priority: P1.** This one is close to free and the player currently has *no
  idea they are on fire*.

#### 6.7d Underwater overlay

- **Bedrock:** `textures/misc/underwater.png` (**16 × 16**, present locally) tiled across
  the screen at low alpha and tinted by the water fog colour, drifting slightly with the
  view.
- **We have:** the **fog**, and it is good — `fluid::kFogColour` / `kFogDistance`
  (`Fluid.hpp:155`), `renderer.setUnderwaterShafts` (`Renderer.hpp:307`), the shader side
  in `deferred.frag:202` and `triangle.frag:416`. What is missing is only the goggle
  texture.
- **Build:** one tiled quad at `alpha 0.1` tinted by `kFogColour`, gated on
  `eyeUnderwater` (already computed, `Main.cpp:4322`). It needs the 16 × 16 tile on the
  sheet and a UV that repeats — `appendSprite` takes a pixel rect, so tiling means either
  4 × 4 quads or a UV outside [0,1] with a repeat sampler.
- **Effort: S · Priority: P2** — the fog already carries most of the information.

#### 6.7e Pumpkin overlay — **blocked on there being no helmet slot**

`textures/misc/pumpkinblur.png` (**256 × 256**, present locally), drawn full-screen at
full alpha. `isCarvedPumpkin` (`Block.hpp:1387`) exists; **there is no armour slot to wear
it in** (§6.3, `GAPS.md` G2.4). One quad once there is.
**Effort: XS · Priority: P3.**

#### 6.7f Nausea warp

- **Bedrock:** a lurching FOV wobble plus a green cast. Java warps the whole frame using
  `textures/misc/nausea.png` (**256 × 256**, present locally).
- **We have:** `Effect::Nausea = 9` with its colour `0x551D4A` (`Effects.hpp:24, 77`) and
  **zero visual consumers**.
- **Build:** this is the **one item in this fragment that is not a HUD quad.** Add a
  `glm::vec4 screenWarp` to `FrameUniforms` (x = amplitude 0…1, y = a wrapped clock) and
  in `tonemap.frag` displace `fragUv` radially:
  `uv += normalize(uv - 0.5) * amplitude * 0.035 * sin(length(uv - 0.5) * 18.0 - clock * 2.5)`.
  Ramp the amplitude in over ~1 s so it does not snap on. `tonemap.frag` already reads
  `sceneColor` by UV, so this is a two-line change plus the uniform.
- **Effort: S · Priority: P3.** Low value: one effect, rarely held.

#### 6.7g Vignette

- **Bedrock/Java:** `textures/misc/vignette.png` (**256 × 256**, present locally)
  multiplied over the frame, strengthening as the light level at the player's position
  falls. It is also the carrier for the Darkness effect and the world border.
- **We have:** nothing. Grep for `vignette` across `game/src` and `engine/` returns zero.
- **Build:** cheapest as a **multiply in `tonemap.frag`** rather than a HUD quad — a HUD
  quad can only *add* darkness over the top and will visibly grey the hotbar. One
  `frame.vignette` float (strength) and `color *= mix(1.0, texture(vignetteTex, uv).r,
  strength)`. Feed the strength from the sky-light value already available at the eye.
- **Effort: S · Priority: P2.** It is the single cheapest thing that makes a cave feel
  like a cave.

### 6.8 Name tags above entities

**What Bedrock does.** A billboarded label above the entity, drawn at a fixed small scale
so it is the same size at any distance, on a **translucent black panel** — the reference's
background is **25 % black** (`0x40000000`), and its opacity is the "Text Background
Opacity" accessibility setting. The **see-through rule** in the reference is a two-pass
one, and it is worth copying exactly: the label is drawn **once with depth testing off**
(so it shows through walls) using the translucent background and dimmed glyphs, and
**again with depth testing on** in solid white — so a visible name reads crisply and an
occluded one reads as a ghost, from the same geometry. Java's cut-off is **64 blocks**
(`distanceToSqr < 4096`), and Java's scale is `0.025` world units per text pixel.

Two Bedrock specifics that change the ranking: only entities with a **custom name** (a
name tag item) carry a permanent label, and *"what am I looking at"* is served by the
**Identify keybind, which prints the name above the hotbar as an item tooltip** — i.e.
§6.6a's channel. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Heads-up_display]

**What we have.** Nothing, and **no world-space text path of any kind**.
`hud::appendText` writes screen-space quads into the UI mesh at a fixed depth;
there is no projection from a world position into HUD space anywhere.
`ItemId::NameTag` (`Item.hpp:331`) is an id with no behaviour. `billboard` appears only
as a world-geometry technique — `Projectile.cpp:337` faces a thrown item at the eye,
`Sky.cpp:35/52` for the sun and moon. `GAPS.md` G9.15 ranks it **M · P2**.

**What must be built.**

1. **Project, do not billboard in a shader.** The one true way that fits this codebase:
   in the HUD builder, take the entity's head position, multiply by the frame's
   view-projection, divide by w, reject `w <= 0` (behind the camera) and anything outside
   `[-1,1]`, and emit ordinary `appendText` + `appendQuad` geometry at the resulting
   screen point. That reuses the entire existing text path and adds no shader, no
   sampler and no vertex format change. `Particles.hpp:109` already documents the same
   choice for particles — *"Built here rather than billboarded in a vertex shader"* — so
   this is the house style, not an invention.
2. **Scale with distance**: `charHeight = kNameHeight / max(1.0f, distance)` clamped so a
   far label does not vanish and a near one does not fill the screen; cut off entirely
   past **64 blocks**.
3. Panel `{0, 0, 0, 0.25f}` sized `textWidth + 2 px` × `charHeight + 2 px`; glyphs white.
4. **The see-through pass is free here and must be said so**: the UI pass has no depth
   attachment, so **everything drawn this way already shows through walls**. Getting the
   reference's *occluded* variant therefore needs the opposite work — a raycast from the
   eye to the entity, and a dimmer colour when it is blocked. `game::raycast`
   (`world/Raycast.hpp`) already exists. **State that in the code, or the next person will
   look for a depth flag that does not exist.**
5. Sort by distance and draw far ones first, so near labels cover far ones.

**Depends on:** the view-projection matrix reaching the HUD builder (it is in
`FrameUniforms`, and `rebuildHud` is a lambda in `main()` with everything in scope);
a name-tag item behaviour for the permanent case.
**Effort: M · Priority: P2** — and note that **§6.6a delivers 80 % of the player-facing
value for XS**, because Bedrock's own answer to "name the thing in front of me" is the
hotbar popup.
