### 6.9 The boss bar — **there is no boss, and this is P3**

**What Bedrock does.** A **182 × 5** bar at the top centre with the boss's name centred
above it. The colour art is all present locally, 23 sprites, every one **182 × 5**:
six colours × background/progress (`pink`, `blue`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`, `purple`,
`white`) plus notched variants at 6, 10, 12 and 20 segments. Sampled from
`purple_progress.png` at x = 90 the five rows are
`#26004A / #7B00EC / #6100B9 / #49008C / #26004A`; the matching background is the same hue
at roughly a quarter of the brightness. Java stacks multiple bars downward on a 19 px
stride (10 px bar block + 9 px name) with the first at y = 12, up to 6 at once. It appears
naturally in exactly three places: a raid, a wither, and the ender dragon.
[https://minecraft.wiki/w/Heads-up_display] · sprite sizes measured locally.

**What we have.** Nothing — grep for `bossbar`, `boss_bar`, `bossBar` across `game/src`
and `engine/` returns **zero hits**. And, decisively: **there is no Nether and no End, so
there is no wither and no dragon**, and there are no raids. There is no creature in the
game with a health-share concept.

**What must be built.** Two sprites (one colour is enough; purple), and
`makeBossBar(name, fraction)` — the width is `kHotbarHalfWidth` again, so the geometry is
already solved. `appendOutlinedText` from §6.2 for the name.

**Depends on:** a boss existing. **Effort: S · Priority: P3.** Honest ranking: this is
the lowest-value item in the fragment. Building it now means a bar that can never appear.

### 6.10 Toasts — **half of it is blocked, half of it is not**

**What Bedrock does.** *"Toasts are text boxes shown when the player unlocks new crafting
recipes… Most of them show up in the top right corner of the screen, and are displayed in
front of effect icons… Up to five toasts can be displayed at once."*
[https://minecraft.wiki/w/Heads-up_display] The frames are present locally: `toast/recipe.png`,
`toast/advancement.png`, `toast/tutorial.png` and `toast/now_playing.png` are all
**160 × 32**, `toast/system.png` is **160 × 64**, and the small icons (`recipe_book`,
`tree`, `wooden_planks`, `mouse`, `right_click`, `movement_keys`, `social_interactions`)
are all **20 × 20**. The `.mcmeta` sidecars give the nine-slice borders exactly:
`now_playing` → `border: 4`, `tutorial` → `border: 3`, `system` →
`{left:17, top:30, right:4, bottom:4}`. Java's timing: slides in from the right over
**600 ms**, holds **5000 ms**, slides out.

**What we have.** No advancement system at all, and **no notification channel of any
kind** — grep for `toast` and `advancement` returns zero. `GAPS.md` G2.20 ranks
achievements **XL · P3**.

**But the recipe toast is not blocked.** `CatalogueState::known` exists and **already
grows as you craft** (`InventoryScreen.hpp:130-175`, filled at `Main.cpp:4028-4032`). A
"New recipes unlocked" toast has a live trigger today. So:

- **Recipe toast:** buildable now. One 160 × 32 nine-sliced frame on the sheet, a small
  queue (`std::deque<Toast>`, max 5), the slide/hold/slide timing above, top-right at
  `y = 1 px` stepping down by 33 px, **in front of the effect icons** (i.e. later in the
  mesh, §6.1). Note it will fight §6.4 for the top-right corner — the reference resolves
  that by putting toasts in front, and so should we.
- **Advancement toast:** blocked on there being no advancements.
- **Music toast** (`now_playing`, top-left): we have **8 overworld tracks**
  (`Sounds.cpp:391-405`) and a track index, so this is also unblocked and is two lines
  once the queue exists.

**Depends on:** the queue itself; nothing else for the recipe and music cases.
**Effort: M · Priority: P3.** The queue is most of the cost, and its only two customers
today are minor. It becomes P1 the moment anything needs to tell the player something.

### 6.11 The debug overlay

This is two separate features and conflating them is why we have neither.

#### 6.11a The coordinate readout — **XS, P0, the single cheapest win in this document**

**What Bedrock does.** *"If enabled in the world options, the player's coordinates and/or
days played will be displayed in a box in the top left of the screen. If both are enabled
at the same time, the position is listed above the number of days played."*
[https://minecraft.wiki/w/Heads-up_display] The format is two decimal places, as visible
in our own local capture
`reference\minecraft-assets-26.2\Minecraft menu and settings screens\Chat_with_coordinates_BE.png`,
which reads **`-985.62  90.82  -2837.73`**. It is **not** part of the debug screen — it is
a normal, always-on HUD element behind a world toggle, on a black panel whose opacity is
the "Text Background Opacity" accessibility setting.

**What we have.** Nineteen rows of developer overlay behind F5 (`DebugOverlay.cpp:90-111`)
and **not one of them is a coordinate**. `GAPS.md` G2.5 says it plainly: *"You cannot tell
where you are."* — **XS · P1**. I would rank it P0.

**Build:** a two-line panel top-left, `charHeight = 8 * kPerReferencePixel`, white with
shadow, on a `{0,0,0,0.4}` panel:
```
Position: -985.62  90.82  -2837.73
Day 14  06:12
```
`player.position` is right there; the day/time come from the same clock that drives the
sky. **Always on** (a settings key can hide it later); it must **not** require F5.
**Effort: XS · Priority: P0.**

#### 6.11b The developer panel — restructured for what is actually broken

**What we have.** `makeDebugOverlay(stats, history, aspect)` — a top-left panel
(`kPanelWidth = 0.56`, `kLineHeight = 0.052`, `kValueColumn = 0.20`) with a frame-time
graph carrying **one guide line at the 60 fps budget** (`kGoodMilliseconds = 16.67f`,
`kGraphMaxMilliseconds = 25.0f`), and 19 rows: `fps, cpu, gpu, biome, air, dist, detail,
tier lag, chunks, meshes, queued, retired, draws, tris, gpu mem, workers, tone F10,
shade G, cloud C`. It refreshes on a 50 ms interval (`Main.cpp:139`). It is a **good
renderer panel** and a **poor world panel**, and every one of `audit.md`'s live findings
is invisible in it.

**What must be built — rows in priority order, chosen against `audit.md`.**

| Row | Value | Why, and what it catches |
|---|---|---|
| `xyz` | `-985.62 90.82 -2837.73` | The one everybody needs |
| `block` | `-986 90 -2838` | Integer cell, for comparing against a saved chunk |
| `chunk` | `-62 5 -178   in 6 10 14` | Chunk coord **and** the local offset. `audit.md` 12.1 (crops never grow above y=32) and 5.2 (revision reset on reload) are both "which chunk am I in" questions |
| `facing` | `north (-Z)  yaw 12.4  pitch -8.1` | |
| `target` | `Oak Log  -986 91 -2840  face +X` | `game::raycast` already returns the cell and the entry direction (`world/Raycast.hpp:10-17`); note it carries **no hit point** (`GAPS.md` G10.8) |
| `light` | `sky 15  block 0   target sky 4 block 7` | `audit.md` 12.1 and the cave-ambience gate (`skyLight <= 2 && y < 40`) are both light questions and both currently unobservable |
| `time` | `day 14  06:12  rain 0.00 thunder 0.00` | `rainAmount`/`thunderAmount` exist at `Main.cpp:6905-6910` |
| **`tick`** | `world 1.8  creatures 0.9  mesh 0.4  hud 0.2 ms` | **This does not exist and is the most valuable new row.** There is no CPU sub-timer anywhere — only whole-frame `deltaSeconds` and `renderer.stats().gpuMilliseconds`. Without it, "the game stutters" has no owner |
| `queues` | `gen 12  mesh 4  light 0  save 2` | `audit.md` 12.2: three of the four queues are missing the unloaded-chunk guard the fourth has. One number each makes that visible |
| `mesh` | `1204 live  8 retired  rev 37  3 stale rejected` | `audit.md` 5.2: a stale in-flight mesh can install permanently. The per-chunk `revision` (`World.hpp:286`) and the job's recorded revision (`World.hpp:300`) already exist; the **count of rejected installs** is derivable and is the direct symptom |
| `ents` | `creatures 84  drops 19  shots 2  particles 940` | All four counters exist and none is shown: `Creatures::count()` (`Creature.hpp:1354`), `ItemEntities::count()` (`ItemEntity.hpp:70`), `Projectiles::count()` (`Projectile.hpp:192`), `Particles::count()` (`Particles.hpp:117`). `audit.md` §13 is almost entirely about creatures |
| `player` | `hp 18/20  food 14  sat 2.4  exh 3.1  air 8.2s  fx 2` | `saturation`/`exhaustion` are documented at `Player.hpp:135-137` as *"the two numbers behind it that never appear on screen"* |
| `hud` | `1420 verts  rebuilt 41/s` | `audit.md` B7: the screen mesh is rebuilt and re-uploaded every frame. A rebuild-rate counter is how anyone would ever notice |
| `chunks` / `draws` / `tris` / `gpu mem` / `workers` | keep | Already correct |
| settings row | keep | `tone F10 / shade G / cloud C` |

**Structural notes.**

1. **Two columns**, not one 25-row list — at `kLineHeight = 0.052` a 25-row panel is
   1.3 units tall, i.e. **65 % of the screen**. World state left, renderer state right.
2. **F5 cycles three states**: off → §6.11a's coordinate box alone → the full panel. That
   makes the coordinate readout reachable without the developer wall of text and matches
   Bedrock's separation of the two.
3. **Give `OverlayStats` the tick sub-timers as real fields** and fill them from
   `std::chrono` spans around the existing update calls in `main()`. This is the only row
   that needs new plumbing rather than a new `Row{}` line.
4. Keep the graph. Add a **second guide line at 33.3 ms** so a 30 fps floor is visible,
   and raise `kGraphMaxMilliseconds` only if it clips.

**Depends on:** nothing for 13 of the 15 rows. **Effort: M · Priority: P1** (the panel);
**XS · P0** for 6.11a alone.

### 6.12 Subtitles for sound events

**What Bedrock does.** *"Closed captions display text for sounds in-game. When turned on,
this lists sounds in the world that are nearby to the player on the right of the screen.
If the sounds are offscreen, '<' or '>' point in the direction the sound is coming from.
As the sound fades away, the text also fades, becoming less white."*
[https://minecraft.wiki/w/Heads-up_display] Bedrock defaults captions **off**, with a
**1.5 s dwell configurable 1–4 s** (already sourced in `GAPS.md` §9.1). The reference's
panel is a black background at ~50 % alpha with 1 px of padding, stacked upward, most
recent at the bottom.

**What we have — the data half is genuinely there, and the naming half is not.**
`core/Sounds.hpp` has `enum class SoundEvent : std::uint8_t` (:31) with **60 enumerators**
(the brief said 57; `Count` is the 61st), `enum class CreatureVoice` (:107) with **35
families** (the brief said 34), and `VoiceState { Idle, Hurt, Death }` (:150).
`Sounds.cpp:12-37` holds `kStems` — **but those are file stems, not subtitles**:
`"dig_stone"`, `"bucket_empty_lava"`, `"levelup"`. **There is no human-readable string for
any event.** And `Sounds::play` / `playGlobal` / `playVoice` all return `void` and take no
listener, so nothing routes a played sound anywhere.

**What must be built.**

1. **A second table parallel to `kStems`**, `constexpr std::array<const char*, Count>
   kCaptions` — `"Block broken"`, `"Bucket emptied"`, `"Player levels up"`,
   `"Chest opens"`. **Add a `static_assert` that the two arrays are the same length**;
   `Sounds.hpp:20-24` already warns that *"a mismatch fails silently as an event that
   never sounds"*, and a caption table has the identical failure mode. Creature voices
   need a second, smaller table: `"Sheep bleats"` × `VoiceState`.
2. **A caption sink.** `Sounds::play` gains an optional
   `CaptionSink* sink` (or the `Sounds` object gains one), pushing
   `{text, worldPosition, ageSeconds}`. Positional events carry a position; `playGlobal`
   does not and must be flagged as directionless.
3. **`makeSubtitles(span<const Caption>, listenerRight, aspect)`**, right-aligned, stacked
   upward from just above the hotbar. Direction: `dot(toSound, listenerRight)` decides
   `<` or `>`; a sound within the view frustum gets neither. Fade the last 0.5 s by
   dropping the colour toward grey, as the reference does — *"becoming less white"*, not
   less opaque.
4. **Dwell 1.5 s**, matching Bedrock's default, off by default behind a
   `subtitles` settings key.
5. Deduplicate: an identical caption arriving while one is live resets its age rather
   than stacking, or walking on gravel produces eight identical lines.

**Depends on:** nothing that does not exist; the sink is a small change to three
functions. `GAPS.md` G9.8 ranks it **M · P2** and notes the genuinely good second reason
for it: *"also the cheapest possible debug view of what the audio layer is actually
doing"* — 16 of 60 events are staged and never fire, and captions would have made that
obvious years earlier.
**Effort: M · Priority: P2.**

---

### 6.13 Screen-space scaling and a GUI-scale setting

**What Bedrock does.** Bedrock has a **"UI Profile"** (Classic / Pocket) plus a scale
slider; Java has **GUI Scale 1…4 or Auto**, where Auto picks the largest integer scale
that keeps the virtual resolution at least **320 × 240**.
[https://minecraft.wiki/w/Settings] Both are, underneath, the same idea: the UI is laid
out in a virtual pixel grid and the grid's size is a setting.

**What we have.** Everything in window-height units, which makes the HUD
**resolution-independent already** — and **neither scalable nor aspect-safe**.
`settings.cfg` parses **44 keys** and not one is a HUD or GUI key
(`core/Settings.hpp`); the only HUD-adjacent ones are `creativeMode` (which hides all
bars, and **defaults to true**) and `renderScale`, whose own doc says *"The interface is
drawn afterwards and is always full size"*. `GAPS.md` G2.11 records the failure: below
about **1.28 : 1** the inventory cards run off both edges.

**The rule to adopt.** One function, one owner, and it reproduces today's size exactly at
16:9:

```cpp
/// One reference GUI pixel, in window-height units.
///
/// The height term is what the HUD has always been. The width term is the
/// reference's own floor - it refuses to let the UI grow past a 320-pixel-wide
/// virtual screen - and is what stops a narrow window running the hotbar off
/// both edges.
float hud::pixel(float aspect, float userScale) {
    constexpr float kVirtualHeight = 266.08f;   // = 2.0f / kPerReferencePixel
    constexpr float kMinVirtualWidth = 320.0f;
    return std::min(2.0f / kVirtualHeight, 2.0f * aspect / kMinVirtualWidth) * userScale;
}
```

At 16:9 this returns `min(0.0075165, 0.011111) = 0.0075165` — **exactly
`kPerReferencePixel` today**, so adopting it changes nothing on a normal window. It begins
to shrink only below **320 / 266 = 1.203 : 1**, which is the correct place.

**What must be built, and the honest cost.**

1. `hud::pixel(aspect, scale)` and a `gui_scale` float settings key (0.5…2.0, default 1.0).
2. **The refactor is the cost.** `kPerReferencePixel`, `kIconSize`, `kIconStep`,
   `kHealthRowY`, `kAirRowY`, `kRowOuterX`, `kHotbarSlotSize`, `kHotbarCentreY`,
   `kHotbarWidth`, `kHotbarTopY` and everything in `StatusBars.cpp` are `constexpr` and
   **four `static_assert`s depend on them** (`StatusBars.cpp:74-84`). Making them runtime
   means those asserts must become either runtime checks in a debug build or `constexpr`
   assertions on the *unscaled* base — **do not simply delete them**; they are the only
   thing that catches the rows colliding.
3. The cheapest useful subset, if the full refactor is not wanted: apply the **aspect
   clamp only**, as a single multiplier computed once per frame in `rebuildHud` and
   threaded into the four `make*` functions. That fixes the real bug (narrow windows) and
   defers the setting.
4. `settings.cfg` is *"read once at startup"* (`Settings.hpp:9-12`), so a live slider
   needs the value re-read on change — but there is no settings screen in this lane
   anyway, so a restart is acceptable for now. **Say so, rather than half-building a live
   path.**

**Depends on:** nothing. **Effort: M** for the setting, **S** for the aspect clamp alone.
**Priority: P2.**

Effort XS ≈ under an hour · S ≈ a few hours · M ≈ a day · L ≈ several days · XL ≈ a
milestone. "Blocked" means the display cannot show anything real until a system that does
not exist is built.

| # | Item | § | Effort | Priority | Blocked on | Why here |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Coordinate + day/time readout, top-left, always on** | 6.11a | **XS** | **P0** | — | You cannot tell where you are. Two lines of text against data already in scope. Bedrock has it as a world toggle, not a debug screen |
| **2** | **Stack count moved to bottom-right, with a shadow, from one owner** | 6.5a | **XS** | **P0** | — | Wrong corner in both draw paths, and fixing it is where the shared item-box owner gets created that items 3 and 8 both need |
| **3** | **Durability bar** | 6.5b | **S** | **P0** | — | `damage` has been tracked, saved and never drawn since tools existed. Highest player-visible value per line of code in the fragment |

**The one to do first:** #3, the durability bar, if you want a single change a player

## 7. Constructed mockups

Seven PNGs in the repo root, all ending `-preview.png` (so `.gitignore` line 22 keeps them
out of version control), all regenerated in one command by `tools\make-ui-mockups.ps1`.

**How they are built.** The script opens `assets\ui\ui-atlas.json`, `ui-palette.json` and
`ui-screens.json` with `ConvertFrom-Json` at startup and prints `read 576 sprites, 221
colours, 24 screens` before drawing anything. Every sprite is blitted from its real file
under `reference\minecraft-assets-26.2\...\textures\gui\`, nine-sliced using the `border`
recorded in the atlas (never a guess), and every position comes from a screens-JSON record.
Composition happens at 1x GUI pixels; every blit multiplies by a single `$Scale = 4` and
uses `InterpolationMode = NearestNeighbor` with `PixelOffsetMode = Half`, so the output is
1920x1080 (480x270 GUI px) for six of them and 1920x2416 for the widget sheet. Nothing is
resampled anywhere.

**Three things worth knowing before you look at any of them:**

- **The text is the real font.** `font\ascii.png` is loaded, its 16x16 grid of 8x8 glyphs is
  sliced, and each glyph's advance is measured by scanning for its rightmost non-transparent
  column (+2; space is 4). Shadow is the glyph re-drawn 1 px down-right at quarter
  brightness, which for white lands on `#3F3F3F` and so matches `text.java.shadow_rule` in
  the palette exactly. **No system font is used anywhere.**
- **Every `DrawImage` shares one `ImageAttributes` with `WrapMode = TileFlipXY`.** Without
  it GDI+ samples one texel outside the source rect and every crop taken from a sheet gets a
  seam. This is why the hotbar and the inventory panel have clean edges.
- **The world behind the pause, HUD, inventory and death screens is constructed, not a
  screenshot** - see 7.8.

---

### 7.1 `ui-mockup-mainmenu-preview.png`

**Shows.** The logo, a four-button column, a version line bottom-left and a disclaimer
bottom-right.

**Assembled from.** `gui\title\minecraft.png` (atlas group `title`, 1024x256, `opaque`
1024x176) blitted into 256x44 GUI px - which at scale 4 is a destination of exactly
1024x176 native, **so the logo is pixel-for-pixel the source file with no resampling at
all**. That is the reason scale 4 was chosen over 3. Buttons are `widget/button` and
`widget/button_highlighted` at the atlas's own 200x20 with nine-slice border 3, positioned
from `screens.widgets.button`. The backdrop is `block\dirt.png` tiled at 32 GUI px and
multiplied by RGB(64,64,64), then `gui\sprites\menu_background.png` (flat black, alpha 64)
tiled on top - which is what that sprite actually is; it is an overlay, not the dirt.

**Real vs drawn.** Everything is reference art except the two text strings.

**Judge.** Whether the logo reads crisply (it should have zero blur - if it looks soft,
something has gone wrong with the scale). Whether the button column spacing feels right:
24 px pitch for the first three, then a 12 px gap before Quit. Whether `Voxel Game - M29`
belongs bottom-left where Minecraft puts its version.

### 7.2 `ui-mockup-settings-preview.png`

**Shows.** A five-tab strip, a scrolling option list with two sliders, one cycler, section
headings, a description line under every row, a scrollbar, and a footer with two buttons.

**Assembled from.** `widget/tab`, `widget/tab_selected` and their `_highlighted` variants
at 130x24 with the atlas's asymmetric border (L2 T2 R2 **B0** - the tab genuinely has no
bottom edge, which is what lets the selected tab bleed into the list). `header_separator`
and `footer_separator` bound the list. Sliders are `widget/slider` + `widget/slider_handle`
(8x20, border L2 T2 R2 B3). The scrollbar is `widget/scroller` on `scroller_background`.
The list background is `background/menu_list_background` (black, alpha 112) over the same
dirt as 7.1.

**Real vs drawn.** All sprites real; text and layout drawn.

**Judge.** Three deliberate departures from `ui-05-menus.md` sec 5.8, all visible here:
1. **The value moved onto the control.** Sec 5.8 asked for `Render Distance: 12 chunks` as a
   left-aligned label with a 200-wide control right-aligned in a 340-wide panel. That does
   not fit - the label measures 140 px in the 8 px font and only 128 px of label room
   exists. The label is now plain (`Render Distance`) and the value rides the slider
   (`12 chunks`) or the button (`On`), which is also what the reference does.
2. **The list background is the reference's own dark list panel, not the classic grey
   bevel.** Sec 5.8 specified a `#C6C6C6` panel with 8 px white labels - white on `#C6C6C6`
   is unreadable. Substituting the real `menu_list_background` keeps every pixel reference
   art and keeps the specified geometry (340 wide, y -88..+88, 24/34 px rows, 98x20 footer
   buttons at y +104).
3. **The description line is 8 px, not 6 px** - `ascii.png` has no 6 px face, so it is the
   same font in `#AAAAAA`.

Also judge: **`Reset to Defaults` is 89 px of text in a 98 px button** - 4 px clearance each
side, tighter than anything in the reference. Either shorten the label or widen the button.
And note the bottom description is clipped by the list bound on purpose, to show scrolling.

### 7.5 `ui-mockup-inventory-preview.png`

**Shows.** The survival inventory with the armour column, the offhand cell, the 2x2 crafting
grid and result, storage, hotbar, a player preview, and a hover tooltip.

**Assembled from** the `inventory` record in `ui-screens.json`: panel 176x166; regions
`armour` (8,8, 1x4, pitch 18), `offhand` (77,62), `crafting_grid` (98,18, 2x2),
`crafting_result` (154,28), `storage` (8,84, 9x3), `hotbar` (8,142, 9x1); art
`player_preview_well` (25,7,51,72) and `recipe_arrow` (135,29,16,13). **The panel is not the
reference PNG** - it is rebuilt from the `panel` record's bevel ladder (black 1 px border,
`#FFFFFF` 2 px top-left, `#C6C6C6` fill, `#555555` 2 px bottom-right) with every slot drawn
by the reversed 1 px ladder (`#373737` top-left, `#8B8B8B` fill, `#FFFFFF` bottom-right,
off-diagonal corners taking the fill). That is deliberate: **it proves the recipe in
`ui-03-palette.md` reproduces the look without shipping Mojang's panel bitmap**, and it is

The **tooltip is real reference art** - `tooltip/background` then `tooltip/frame`,
nine-sliced at borders 9 and 10, `frame` being the one sprite in the whole atlas with
`stretchInner: true`. Height comes from the Java formula in `screens.widgets.tooltip`:
`8` for one line, else `8 + 2 + (n-1)*10`, box expanded by margin 9. The hover highlight is
`container/slot_highlight_back` + `_front` at 24x24, drawn at item origin -4,-4.

**Real vs drawn.** Tooltip, highlight, slot empty-icons (`container/slot/leggings` in the
empty armour row) and every item texture are real. Panel and slots are drawn from the
palette recipe. The player figure is a flat paper doll composited from `steve.png` UV rects.

**Judge.** (a) Does the rebuilt panel look identical to the reference one to your eye - if
it does, the palette recipe is confirmed and we never need the bitmap. (b) The armour
column: helmet / chestplate / **empty leggings showing its slot icon** / boots, which is the
whole point of including it. (c) The offhand cell at (77,62) - it is only 14 px below the
crafting grid and may feel tight. (d) The tooltip's four-line layout: name, durability,
`When in main hand:` in grey, then an attribute line in blue.

### 7.6 `ui-mockup-death-preview.png`

**Shows.** `You Died!` at 3x (24 px), the cause line, an amber bed-status line, Respawn and
Title Screen, and a score line.

**Assembled from.** `widget/button` / `button_highlighted`; the overlay is a translucent
dark-red rect over the world, which is why it reads mauve where the sky shows through.

**Real vs drawn.** Buttons and font real; the red wash and the world are drawn.

**Judge.** Whether 3x is the right title size (Minecraft uses 2x for `You Died!` and relies
on the red wash for weight - 3x here is a deliberate escalation from `ui-05-menus.md` sec
5.9). Whether the amber `Your bed was missing or blocked.` line earns its place above the
buttons or belongs below them.

---

### 7.7 `ui-mockup-widgets-preview.png` - the parts catalogue

**Shows.** Every reusable part in one 480x604 GUI-px sheet, each with a caption naming its
atlas id, size and nine-slice border. Seven sections:

| Section | Contents |
|---|---|
| Button | normal, hover (label `#FFFFA0`), disabled (**border 1, not 3** - the atlas says so), and a 98x20 Done/Cancel pair from the same sprite re-sliced |
| Slider | track + handle, normal and hover, both sprites swapping together |
| Text field | idle with dark-grey placeholder, focused with caret |
| Checkbox | off / off-hover / on / on-hover, plus `cross`, `locked`, `unlocked`, and both page arrows |
| Tab | unselected, unselected-hover, selected, selected-hover - the B0 border is visible on the selected pair |
| Scrollbar, panel, popup, tooltip | `widget/scroller`, the Bedrock bar rebuilt three-slice, the classic bevel, `popup/background` (nine-slice 6), `tooltip/background` + `frame` |
| Slot | empty, stack count, durability 13x2, hover, empty-slot icon, disabled, uncraftable (Bedrock crop), output well, recipe 25x25, recipe-no-stock |
| Hotbar and bars | a live hotbar plus one of every bar icon at 1x |

**Real vs drawn.** Everything except the captions is reference art blitted at its own size.

**Judge.** This is the one to spend time on, because everything else is assembled from it.
Specifically: is the **disabled button** distinguishable enough at a glance (it is the real
`button_disabled` sprite, and it is subtle); do the **four tab states** read as four states;
and is the **uncraftable / output-well** pair - the only two Bedrock crops in the set -
stylistically compatible with the Java parts sitting beside them. If they are not, they
should be redrawn from the classic slot recipe with a red tint instead.

---

### 7.8 What could not be made convincing

**The world behind four of the screens is a hand-built cross-section, not the game.** It is
a sine-driven height profile of real `grass_block_side` / `dirt` / `stone` / `cobblestone` /
`coal_ore` / `oak_log` / tinted `oak_leaves` tiles with a depth-based black gradient and two
trees. It exists only so the dim layers, the HUD contrast and the tooltip legibility can be
judged against something. **It reads as a side-scroller, not as a first-person voxel world**,
and no amount of tile arrangement fixes that - it needs an actual screenshot. If the
developer drops one in, the script has a single function (`Get-WorldBackdrop`) to replace.
Clouds are plain white rectangles, which is the weakest thing on the sheet.

**Block items are flat faces, not 3D cube icons.** Minecraft renders an item-form block as
an isometric cube built from three faces at three brightnesses. Doing that properly needs a
transform per face and a per-face shade table; here a block item is just its side texture.
Look at cobblestone, planks, sand and the crafting table result in 7.5 - they are the
clearest tell that these are mockups. This is a real feature we will have to build (and it
is one of the four draw paths named in the `CLAUDE.md` opening box).

**The player preview is a flat paper doll.** Head, body, two arms and two legs cut as UV
rects from `entity\player\wide\steve.png` and stacked. No perspective, no head tracking, no
overlay layer. It is recognisably Steve and nothing more.

**No splash text on the main menu.** The reference draws it rotated, and rotating means
resampling, which means blur, which fails the one rule that matters here. It would need to
be pre-rendered rotated and blitted.

**No enchantment glint, no cooldown sweep, no item-pickup animation.** All three are
animated or shader effects and a still frame cannot show them honestly.

**Nine-slice inner regions are tiled, not stretched** (except `tooltip/frame`, which the
atlas marks `stretchInner`). That is what the reference does and it never resamples - but it
means a sprite whose centre is a gradient would band. None of the ones used here are.

**The 6 px description font does not exist.** Called out in 7.2, repeated here because it
affects any future screen that wanted a smaller secondary line: `ascii.png` is 8 px and that
is the only size we have without authoring a second font.
